Comprehension:
Punjab’s drug problem is so severe that every effort aimed at stemming the rot deserves praise. It is commendable that many Punjabi celebrities — from renowned actors and singers to outstanding sportspersons — have exhorted people of the state to shun drugs and restore the health of Punjabi youth. Amid the continuing police crackdown on drugs, the appeal by these popular figures is expected to bolster the fight against the menace, which has been eating into the state’s vitals for the past two decades or so. The involvement of India’s hockey team captain Harmanpreet Singh and cricketers Harmanpreet Kaur and Arshdeep Singh in the ‘nasha-mukt Punjab’ movement is particularly significant. Fitness is a key prerequisite for sporting success, and champions belonging to the state can inspire youngsters to stay away from drugs and take up sports as a career or a hobby. 
 As far as Punjabi performers are concerned, they need to be more vocal in condemning singers, actors and filmmakers who glorify alcohol consumption and violence. Those who promote the lethal cocktail of drugs and guns should be called out unequivocally. The cleansing and course correction have to start within the Punjabi film and music industry. 
 Hindi movie Udta Punjab (2016) drew the nation’s attention to the border state’s drug crisis. The state government of the day contended that Punjab was wrongly portrayed as a drug haven, but there were many observers who saw in it a glimpse of the ground situation. Eight years later, the famed land of farmers and soldiers is still struggling to erase the drug taint and combat narco terror. Apart from the wholehearted support of stars, Punjab needs greater assistance from the Centre. Curbing cross-border smuggling of contraband holds the key to snapping the supply chain. A multi-pronged strategy — combining stringent law enforcement with public awareness campaigns — can do Punjab a world of good. 
 What is the tone of the passage?
cpomains29.explanation:
A)Urgent 
 The tone of the passage is urgent because it highlights the severity of Punjab's drug problem and the immediate need for action. The passage emphasizes the necessity of various efforts, including police crackdowns, celebrity involvement, and government assistance to combat the drug menace, indicating the urgency of the situation. 
 B. Optimistic is incorrect because while the passage does commend efforts to fight drugs, it does not primarily focus on hope or positive outcomes; instead, it emphasizes the critical need for action. 
 C. Celebratory is incorrect because the passage does not celebrate any achievements. It rather focuses on the ongoing challenges and the serious issue at hand. 
 D. Humorous is incorrect because the passage addresses a serious issue in a serious tone. There is no humor in the discussion of Punjab’s drug crisis.

Comprehension:
Who has a tail that never stops wagging, ears that perk up at the mention of a walk or chicken, and a brain that can remember the names of toys, years after those toys get lost and/or chewed up and thrown out? As those who have spent any time with one would attest, the good boys and girls of the world — doggos and puppers, as they are known on the internet — are also very clever boys and girls. A study at the Eotvos Lorand University in Hungary has found that dogs can store up to a dozen object names in their long-term memory, correctly identifying toys that they have not seen in two years. 
 For scientists, this is an important finding which could lead to a greater understanding of the parts of the brain connected to the mechanics and evolution of language, given the connection between long-term memory and linguistic skills. The fact that dogs are capable of such feats of memory — on top of their incredible emotional intelligence and ability to “read” humans — also opens up greater possibilities for their deployment as service and emotional support animals, as well as in search and rescue operations. 
 Dogs, of course, are not unique in their startling displays of intelligence — other species, like squirrels, octopi, rats and crows, too have demonstrated problem-solving skills and the ability to retrieve information from their long-term memory. What makes canine intelligence special, however, is that it seems to have developed as a response to the close, millennia-long relationship between dogs and humans. In other words, it is because of domestication that puppies, even when they’re mere weeks old, are better at understanding humans and using that knowledge to infer information about the environment, like where the treats are hidden. So humans can, perhaps, claim some credit for the intelligence of their furry companions. But dogs’ seemingly unending store of love and loyalty? That’s entirely down to their own selves. 
 What is the tone of the passage?
cpomains29.explanation:
D)Informative 
 The passage gives factual information about the intelligence of dogs, including details about scientific studies and findings, without inserting personal opinion or humor. The focus is on educating the reader. 
 A: This is incorrect because the passage doesn't analyze or break down data or complex arguments. It focuses on presenting facts and findings. 
 B: This is incorrect because the tone is not light-hearted or meant to make the reader laugh. The language is straightforward and factual. 
 C: This is incorrect because the passage doesn't criticize or evaluate something negatively. It is neutral and focused on presenting information.

 a) Sentence starts with “Recently”, which sets a temporal context, indicating when the event happened. (Sentence की शुरुआत “Recently” से होती है, जो घटना के समय (time context) को दर्शाता है कि यह घटना हाल ही में हुई है।) 
 d) Next, “the Mayor” is introduced as the subject of the sentence. इसके बाद “the Mayor” आता है, जो sentence का subject है, यानी यह बताता है कि यह घटना Mayor के बारे में है। 
 e) The phrase “of the picturesque Santorini” comes next, adding a descriptive detail about the Mayor's location. फिर “of the picturesque Santorini” आता है, जो Mayor की location के बारे में बताता है, यानी Santorini, एक सुंदर स्थान है।

 f) “had to declare” follows the subject to indicate the action the Mayor took. “had to declare” आता है, जो Mayor द्वारा की गई action को इंगित करता है, यानी उन्हें एक घोषणा करनी पड़ी। 
 i) “an emergency” completes the action, explaining what the Mayor had to declare. “an emergency” इस action को पूरा करता है, जो बताता है कि Mayor ने आपातकाल की घोषणा की थी। 
 h) “as 17000 tourists” provides the reason for the emergency declaration. “as 17000 tourists” बताता है कि इस आपातकाल की घोषणा का कारण क्या था – 17,000 पर्यटकों (tourists) की मौजूदगी। 
 b) “descended” follows to indicate what the tourists did, i.e., descended onto the island. इसके बाद “descended” आता है, जो बताता है कि पर्यटक Santorini द्वीप पर आ गए (arrived) थे। 
 g) “on the island” specifies where the tourists arrived. “on the island” यह स्पष्ट करता है कि पर्यटक द्वीप पर कहां आए थे।in” introduces a specific location. “in” आगे specific location का परिचय देता है। 
 c) Finally, “one day” concludes the sentence, providing an additional time context. अंत में “one day” आता है, जो एक अतिरिक्त time context देता है कि यह सब एक ही दिन में हुआ।

cpomains30.word:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence. 
 A. Well, 60 years after Bombay bid adieu to its trams (1964), the passenger tramway in Kolkata, India’s last remaining network, has come to an end 151 years after its introduction. 
 B. Contemporary Turkish playwright, novelist and thinker Mehmet Murat ildan may be a little bit fascinated with trams. 
 C. A small stretch from Maidan to the Esplanade, however, will be retained as a heritage for tram lovers for occasional time-machine rides. 
 D. West Bengal’s administrative authorities contend that trams cause unnecessary congestion on roads that are increasingly difficult to manage. 
 E. He said, “Cities who do not have trams always look less literary, less poetic, and less mysterious!”
cpomains30.explanation:
C) BEADC 
 Bsentence से paragraph की शुरुआत होती है क्योंकि इसमें Mehmet Murat Ildan का परिचय दिया गया है, जो एक Turkish playwright, novelist, और thinker हैं। इसमें बताया गया है कि Ildan ट्रामों के प्रति काफी fascinated हैं। 
 E logically Bके बाद आता है क्योंकि इसमें Mehmet Murat Ildan का quote दिया गया है, जिसमें वह कहते हैं कि जिन शहरों में ट्राम नहीं होतीं, वे कम “literary, poetic, and mysterious” लगते हैं। यह ट्रामों के poetic और symbolic महत्व को highlight करता है। 
 A, Eके बाद आता है क्योंकि यह ट्रामों के संदर्भ को India से जोड़ता है। यह बताता है कि Bombay में ट्राम का अंत हो गया था और Kolkata में 151 साल बाद आखिरकार ट्राम नेटवर्क बंद हो गया, जो भारत का आखिरी बचा हुआ ट्राम नेटवर्क था। यह ट्राम के इतिहास और वर्तमान स्थिति को विस्तार से बताता है। 
 Dइसके बाद आता है क्योंकि यह West Bengal’s authorities का दृष्टिकोण बताता है, जो मानते हैं कि ट्रामें सड़कों पर “congestion” का कारण बनती हैं और उन्हें manage करना मुश्किल हो जाता है। यह ट्रामों के decline का practical कारण देता है। 
 C paragraphको conclude करता है, यह बताते हुए कि Maidan से Esplanade तक एक छोटा हिस्सा heritage के रूप में रखा जाएगा ताकि tram lovers कभी-कभी इस historical ride का आनंद ले सकें। यह पूरे paragraph को एक nostalgic और thoughtful conclusion देता है। 
 Explanation in English: 
 B + E:B introduces the subject (Mehmet Murat Ildan), and E gives his quote. The subject (Mehmet Murat Ildan) is continued from B into E through “he said.” 
 E + A:A shifts the focus from Ildan’s opinion to a factual statement about trams in India. A directly connects with E by continuing the discussion about trams but now focusing on the real-life situation in Kolkata. 
 A + D:D follows A by explaining why trams were discontinued, connecting the factual situation in A with the reasoning in D. 
 D + C:C provides a contrast to D by giving an exception to the closure. It connects by showing that despite the closure, a small stretch will be retained for heritage purposes.

It is not ______1_____that fiscal federalism finds a _____2______ place in judicial discourse. The Supreme Court judgment, holding by an overwhelming majority of 8:1 that the States can tax mineral rights and mineral-bearing lands, _____3_____ a truly landmark ruling, as it protects _____4_____ legislative domain from interference by Parliament. For decades, it was believed that the States were _____5_____of their power to impose any tax on mineral resources extracted from their land because of the prevalence of a central law, the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957. Even though the right to tax mineral rights is conferred _____6______ the States through Entry 50 in the State List of the Seventh Schedule, it was made “subject to any limitations imposed by Parliament by law relating to mineral development”. The Union government argued that the very existence of its 1957 law was a limitation on the States’ power to tax mineral rights, but Chief Justice of India, Dr. D.Y. Chandrachud, writing for the Bench, examined the Act’s provisions to _____7_____that it contained no such limitation. The royalty ______8______ by the 1957 Act was Held to be not a tax at all. The Union was hoping that once royalty was accepted as a tax, it would wholly occupy the field and thus remove the States’ scope for taxing mineral rights. _____9______, the Court chose to see royalty as a contractual consideration for enjoyment of mineral rights. Also, it ____10______that States could tax mineral-bearing lands under Entry 49, a general power to tax lands. 
 Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
cpomains30.explanation:
C) 'Often'का use होगा क्योंकि "often" का अर्थ होता है 'अक्सर' या 'बार-बार', जो इस संदर्भ में उपयुक्त है। Passage में यह बताया गया है कि fiscal federalism (राजकोषीय संघवाद) का न्यायिक प्रवचन में बार-बार उल्लेख होता है, जिससे यह सिद्ध होता है कि यह कोई असामान्य या दुर्लभ घटना नहीं है। जबकि 'Very' का अर्थ है 'बहुत', जो मात्रा को व्यक्त करता है, 'Mostly' का अर्थ है 'ज्यादातर', जो सामान्यीकृत विवरण देने के लिए प्रयोग होता है, और 'Vastly' का अर्थ है 'विशाल रूप से', जो इस संदर्भ में सही नहीं है। 
 'Often' will be used because it means 'frequently' or 'many times,' which fits here as the passage indicates that fiscal federalism is a recurring topic in judicial discourse, making it suitable. Whereas, 'Very' expresses intensity or degree, 'Mostly' implies generalization, and 'Vastly' means 'to a great extent,' which don't fit in this context.

Comprehension:
The world is a wonderful place to live in. Technology has made it even more alluring. But behind the facade of fabulous lifestyles and high-end cars are loneliness, depression and sorrow. Even those who have reached the pinnacle of success suffer from anxiety, failed relationships and mental health issues. 
 The Bhagwad Gita provides a technique for life that enables us to live ordinary lives in an extraordinary way. The single most important determinant of success, happiness, and growth is the intellect. The mind is a flow of thought, the domain of emotions, feelings, and impulses. The intellect has the ability to discern, discriminate between pairs of opposites, and decide. A well-fortified intellect stands apart from emotions, from the likes and dislikes of the mind, and thinks clearly. 
 Look within. Shift your gaze from the world to yourself. When you look at yourself objectively, you see the demons within. You begin to change the way you think, feel, and act, and the results are magical. 
 You think happiness lies out there in the world, in the malls of the world. If happiness were truly in the world, the same object should give the same quantum of happiness to all. This does not happen. Are we barking up the wrong tree? 
 We seek instant gratification. Swipe, and you get what you want in a jiffy. But that which gives instant joy gives sorrow in the long run. Junk food is delicious. However, too much of it leads to ill health. It may feel good to be nasty to people, but it makes for a lonely life later. In the rush for instant pleasure, we sign up for a life of unhappiness. 
 This does not mean you live a life of pain and self-denial. Enjoy instant pleasure, but also invest in your long-term happiness. Wake up early and exercise most days, but sleep in late once in a while. 
 We all want success in life. We do not realise that perfection lies within. Why are you working? If it is only for personal profit and pleasure, you become mediocre. Motivated by a higher ideal you become amazingly successful. Don Bradman did not play cricket for money. Ustad Bismillah Khan played the shehnai for the love of it. Einstein was dedicated to Physics. 
 The Bhagwad Gita says, “Work in a spirit of yajna, service, and sacrifice for a higher ideal. Go beyond petty, self-serving interests and dedicate your actions to your company, community, or country. Your mind remains calm, your intellect is sharp, and your actions brilliant. You achieve outstanding success. All unselfish people are happy. And they evolve spiritually, too.” 
 Expand your circle of love, and you feel connected. Feel one with people, and life becomes extraordinary. Your loved ones go well beyond the routine to do things for you. You experience the incredible result of collective, cooperative effort. The larger your circle of love, the greater the happiness. 
 Lastly, understand that everything in the world is impermanent. Search for the permanent, that which always remains with you. The wise do not bother with the passing, ephemeral joys of life. Seek the eternal and attain it. Then you become truly extraordinary.​

 The passage focuses on how individuals can transform their lives for the better by applying wisdom from the Bhagavad Gita and understanding that success and happiness lie within. It highlights positive steps like self-improvement, seeking higher ideals, and expanding love, making the tone optimistic. 
 B. Incorrect, because the passage does not dwell on negative outcomes. It acknowledges challenges such as loneliness and sorrow but offers hope and solutions, rather than focusing on despair.

Comprehension:
The recent tragic death of a young woman working for a prestigious firm has evoked anguish, with so much being discussed about having a reasonable work-life balance. This highly qualified individual worked for a firm with presumably world-class corporate governance. However, there is only so much the human body can handle; lack of sleep, rest, and proper nutrition can destroy health. It is the responsibility of society and the state to protect the citizens when these things are violated. 
 People have pointed out that the working environment in modern offices has become toxic and unhealthy. Perhaps they are right. But these are times of great revival in the nation, and a demanding work environment is an inescapable reality. This is the reality of the challenges, opportunities and rewards of the times, and there is only so much the state can do to regulate the modern workplace. So, it’s crucial that we, as individuals, take matters into our own hands to protect ourselves and our young. 
 The first is to examine the work environment. A famous leader of our country was recently asked about what he does to relax, especially with the mind-boggling stress his job brings. His answer is revelatory and inspirational. He said his work was relaxation, an answer that aligned with India’s ethos. After all, our forefathers were emperors, merchants and scholars, and we can find their imprints across the globe. Even the most nationalistic Indians of today cannot claim to have surpassed their achievements. They did not have to resort to finding a balance because dharm governed their lives. Somewhere, in the mad rush for modernity and prosperity, we have abandoned principles based on ancient Indic wisdom, so work and workplaces have become so stressful. 
 But what about life after work, which is supposed to act as a counterbalance? A cursory examination reveals that we are not doing enough to unwind; our activities are contrary. If work brings stress, we should do those things that counteract it. Watching movies on a mobile phone, binge shopping, or binge eating are not solutions. It is not enough to hit the gym; the workplace stress builds up during the day, and even thinking about it in the evening hampers recovery – the mind has to take a meaningful break. 
 According to a recent article in Harvard Business Review, one method is to detach psychologically from work. The mind has to be engaged in something removed from work. The authors suggest practising mindfulness as a solution. 
 What did our forefathers do? One way was to practise evening sandhya, a practice prevalent throughout the land. It is performed at dusk, a time for transitioning from day activities to contemplation, of connecting with the Divine. In the past, everyone did it as dharm. The bindings of dharm are no longer applicable today. However, people can embrace proven methods from the past because they can help solve today’s problems. 
 The key is to engage the mind and to train it to stay engaged. In this field, we can be proud of inheriting humanity’s treasure trove of knowledge. The time has come to unearth the eternal treasures and profit from them.​

cpomains30.word:
Comprehension:
The recent tragic death of a young woman working for a prestigious firm has evoked anguish, with so much being discussed about having a reasonable work-life balance. This highly qualified individual worked for a firm with presumably world-class corporate governance. However, there is only so much the human body can handle; lack of sleep, rest, and proper nutrition can destroy health. It is the responsibility of society and the state to protect the citizens when these things are violated. 
 People have pointed out that the working environment in modern offices has become toxic and unhealthy. Perhaps they are right. But these are times of great revival in the nation, and a demanding work environment is an inescapable reality. This is the reality of the challenges, opportunities and rewards of the times, and there is only so much the state can do to regulate the modern workplace. So, it’s crucial that we, as individuals, take matters into our own hands to protect ourselves and our young. 
 The first is to examine the work environment. A famous leader of our country was recently asked about what he does to relax, especially with the mind-boggling stress his job brings. His answer is revelatory and inspirational. He said his work was relaxation, an answer that aligned with India’s ethos. After all, our forefathers were emperors, merchants and scholars, and we can find their imprints across the globe. Even the most nationalistic Indians of today cannot claim to have surpassed their achievements. They did not have to resort to finding a balance because dharm governed their lives. Somewhere, in the mad rush for modernity and prosperity, we have abandoned principles based on ancient Indic wisdom, so work and workplaces have become so stressful. 
 But what about life after work, which is supposed to act as a counterbalance? A cursory examination reveals that we are not doing enough to unwind; our activities are contrary. If work brings stress, we should do those things that counteract it. Watching movies on a mobile phone, binge shopping, or binge eating are not solutions. It is not enough to hit the gym; the workplace stress builds up during the day, and even thinking about it in the evening hampers recovery – the mind has to take a meaningful break. 
 According to a recent article in Harvard Business Review, one method is to detach psychologically from work. The mind has to be engaged in something removed from work. The authors suggest practising mindfulness as a solution. 
 What did our forefathers do? One way was to practise evening sandhya, a practice prevalent throughout the land. It is performed at dusk, a time for transitioning from day activities to contemplation, of connecting with the Divine. In the past, everyone did it as dharm. The bindings of dharm are no longer applicable today. However, people can embrace proven methods from the past because they can help solve today’s problems. 
 The key is to engage the mind and to train it to stay engaged. In this field, we can be proud of inheriting humanity’s treasure trove of knowledge. The time has come to unearth the eternal treasures and profit from them.​ 
 Which of the following best reflects the author's stance on the work-life balance?
options: It is impossible to achieve a work-life balance in today's fast-paced world.
Individuals must take personal responsibility to create their own work-life balance.
The government should strictly regulate workplaces to ensure a balanced lifestyle.
Modern work environments are balanced and do not cause any harm to individuals.
cpomains30.explanation:
B) Individuals must take personal responsibility to create their own work-life balance. 
 A is incorrect because the author does not claim that work-life balance is impossible but suggests it is achievable through personal efforts. 
 C is incorrect because while the author mentions the state has a role, they emphasize that there’s only so much the government can do, shifting the onus onto individuals. 
 D is incorrect because the passage clearly discusses the toxicity and stress of modern work environments, suggesting they are indeed harmful. 
 B is correct because the author advocates for personal responsibility in managing work-life balance, as seen in the recommendation to take control of one’s stress management.

cpomains30.word:
Comprehension:
No one says, “I do not want to be happy.” Everyone is looking for happiness in different places. Consuming as much as possible is also a source of happiness, points out Prof Samdhong Rinpoche, speaking at the ‘Spirit of Tibet’ festival held in Delhi recently. Anything that brings temporary happiness like possession of material goods, will only create more greed, and an unending circle of joy and sorrow. Your happiness should not become the cause of unhappiness. To define happiness is a slippery task as each one of us has a different notion of happiness. Happiness is really a mindset, a mental attitude. Your body may experience disease and pain, while your mind might be happy. Conversely, your body may be fit and healthy, but your mind is filled with unhappiness due to turmoil. Therefore, you need to discover what makes you unhappy and overcome that root cause. Very often, the root cause of unhappiness is avidya, ignorance. To cultivate inner wisdom, you need to be disciplined, in mind and body. Happiness is not a set of emotions but a cessation of all negative emotions. When you are at peace, free of contamination, that is happiness. Sustainable happiness comes with nirvana. But most people do not experience nirvana. 
 Buddhists talk of equality of all sentient beings on three basic grounds. First, no living being wants unhappiness. Second, the basic nature of consciousness in every individual is the same. Everyone has the right to seek happiness and avoid unhappiness. Third, every individual has the potential to evolve to buddha nature. 
 Since we are all equal, an individual’s approach to all sentient beings has to be with a sense of equilibrium. The basis of happiness is understanding equanimity, so that one can feel the oneness that is built into the web of life. Shantideva asks, why worry about problems, why not seek remedies instead? Prof Samdhong Rinpoche talked of how unfulfilled desires, fear, anxiety, jealousy and anger are all causes of unhappiness. If anger is the cause of your discomfort, find out the root cause of that anger and try to overcome it. Learn to differentiate between actor and action. The Buddha did not see the person with negative emotions as the enemy; he recognised kleshas, negativities, as enemy. 
 In other words, hate the sin but love the sinner. Avoid violent action. Only something that is the opposite nature of fire, can put out the fire. Overcome anger with compassion, violence with love. Under the complete influence of negative emotions, the actor has no freedom and so no control over himself. Hence, we need to address the cause and not the symptom. 
 When you react in anger or anxiety, you become its ally and the first outcome will be violence. Unless you are compassionate, you cannot counter kleshas. Understand your needs. This is important because you are indoctrinated to need or want more than is necessary. 
 Gandhiji promoted control of oneself. This will give you freedom to think and recognise who you are. When you compare yourself with others, you forget your true identity and personality. Never get brainwashed into believing what others say about you, that you are stupid or a coward. Free your mind. Be happy. 
 What is the tone of the passage?
cpomains30.explanation:
A)Philosophical 
 A. This is the correct answer because the passage delves deeply into the nature of happiness and inner peace, discussing concepts like nirvana, equanimity, and self-control, which are hallmarks of philosophical discourse. 
 B. Incorrect. Although the passage examines different sources of happiness, it does so without harsh judgment or critique. The tone is more contemplative than critical. 
 C. Incorrect. The passage does not present an overly positive view but rather a balanced, neutral stance on achieving happiness through discipline and understanding. 
 D: Incorrect. The passage maintains a calm and reflective tone throughout, without any indication of aggression or hostility.

If anger is the cause of your discomfort, find out the root cause of that anger and try to overcome it. Learn to differentiate between actor and action. The Buddha did not see the person with negative emotions as the enemy; he recognised kleshas, negativities, as enemy. 
 In other words, hate the sin but love the sinner. Avoid violent action. Only something that is the opposite nature of fire, can put out the fire. Overcome anger with compassion, violence with love. Under the complete influence of negative emotions, the actor has no freedom and so no control over himself. Hence, we need to address the cause and not the symptom. 
 When you react in anger or anxiety, you become its ally and the first outcome will be violence. Unless you are compassionate, you cannot counter kleshas. Understand your needs. This is important because you are indoctrinated to need or want more than is necessary. 
 Gandhiji promoted control of oneself. This will give you freedom to think and recognise who you are. When you compare yourself with others, you forget your true identity and personality. Never get brainwashed into believing what others say about you, that you are stupid or a coward. Free your mind. Be happy.

 ii Unhappiness arises from negative emotions like anger and jealousy, and it is crucial to understand and address these emotions to attain true happiness. 
 iii Practicing anger and violence helps one understand the cause of their negative emotions and thus overcome them. 
 iv Compassion, self-control, and understanding one’s true needs are the key methods to counter negative emotions and find happiness.
cpomains30.explanation:
B) ii and iv 
 ii and iv are correct: Both options ii and iv focus on the passage’s emphasis on identifying the root causes of negative emotions (like anger and jealousy) and using compassion, self-control, and self-understanding to overcome them. This aligns perfectly with the passage’s central idea. 
 i is incorrect: It suggests that external circumstances are the primary cause of unhappiness, which is not discussed in the passage. 
 iii is incorrect: It misinterprets the passage by suggesting that practicing negative emotions can help overcome them, which contradicts the author's message.

Comprehension: 
 India has solidified its defence partnership with the United States through two pivotal agreements, signaling a deepening American commitment to South Asia at a time when China's military influence is expanding across the region. The agreements, secured during Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's recent four-day visit to the United States, include a Security of Supply Arrangement (SOSA) and a Memorandum of Agreement on the Assignment of Liaison Officers. These developments underscore a significant shift in the dynamics of Indo-US relations, with both nations moving closer in their defence cooperation. The SOSA, a non-binding bilateral pact, is designed to prioritise support for defence-related goods and services between the two countries. This agreement is particularly crucial in addressing supply chain vulnerabilities that are critical to national security. Under the SOSA, India will receive assurances from Washington’s Defence Priorities and Allocations System, while Indian companies will provide priority support to the United States. India's inclusion in the elite group of 18 SOSA partners, which includes nations like Australia, Canada, and Britain, marks a significant step in defence cooperation. 
 In effect it means if either of two nations ended up in combat with an adversary, the SOSA could help accelerate the delivery of crucial weapons and materials required for defence, thereby ensuring robust supply chains in times of crisis. India and the United States have already established several key strategic agreements, including the Logistics Exchange Memorandum of Agreement (LEMOA) signed in 2016 and real-time intelligence sharing since 2018 under the Communications Compatibility and Security Agreement (COMCASA). These agreements, alongside the new SOSA, create a framework for expedited deliveries of contracted goods and services, potentially streamlining defence commerce between the two nations. In 2019, the signing of the Industrial Security Annex marked another significant step, allowing the sharing of classified US information with private Indian defence firms-a departure from previous restrictions. The Reciprocal Defence Procurement Agreement could further streamline defence commerce, enabling private companies in both countries to bid on each other's contracts. Indeed, a technologically advanced Indian military aligns with American interests. The recent Indo-US defence agreements mark a significant milestone in the evolving relationship between the two nations. As China's influence continues to grow across South Asia, particularly in Islamabad and the Maldives, these agreements provide a foundation for enhanced collaboration and a shared commitment to regional stability. With these developments, India and the United States are poised to further deepen their defence ties, building a partnership that could play a crucial role in shaping the future of the region. 
 Which of the following statements best fills the gap in the passage in relation to India's strategic goals through the SOSA agreement?
options: The SOSA agreement will provide India with advanced military technologies from the United States.
The SOSA agreement will allow India to receive priority support in defence-related goods during crises.
The SOSA agreement primarily focuses on intelligence sharing between the two nations.
The SOSA agreement aims at improving economic trade between India and the United States.
cpomains30.explanation:
B) B is the correct answer because the SOSA agreement is described as focusing on prioritising support for defence-related goods and services. The passage emphasizes how this is crucial for addressing supply chain vulnerabilities, which are related to India's security needs during crises. 
 A is incorrect because the passage does not mention advanced military technology as the primary benefit of the agreement. It focuses on goods and services rather than technology transfer. 
 C is incorrect because intelligence sharing is not mentioned in the passage. The focus is more on supply chain cooperation rather than intelligence. 
 D is incorrect because the agreement is about defence-related priorities, not about improving economic trade between the nations.

cpomains30.word:
Comprehension:
After a year of frosty exchanges and declining relations, India and Canada have declared diplomatic war, as India’s Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) revealed this week that the Canadian government had sought to investigate and even interrogate the Indian High Commissioner and five other diplomats, naming them “persons of interest” for the killing of Khalistani activist Hardeep Singh Nijjar. Mr. Nijjar, who was shot dead in June 2023 in British Columbia, was wanted by India. In a press conference, the Canadian police (RCMP) detailed their suspicions that the Indian diplomats were somehow involved with an Indian criminal network they believe is responsible for the killing, as well in the targeting of some in the Indian diaspora. The Canadian Ministry of Foreign Affairs has alleged political interference by India’s diplomats, something hitherto it had accused China of. India’s MEA has called the charges “preposterous”, accusing Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau of orchestrating the investigations for political gain with a pro-separatist Khalistani votebank, given his record-low ratings ahead of the 2025 general election. India also accused what it called the Canadian “regime” for providing space to “violent extremists and terrorists to ... intimidate Indian diplomats and community leaders...”, in the name of free speech. Delhi and Ottawa have each expelled six diplomats. With the reduced staff strength in the High Commissions in both capitals and an outraged India reserving the right to further action, it could well mean drastic cuts in visas and curtailed direct travel links. 
 With the die cast for worsening ties, New Delhi must consider carefully the impact of its next steps not only on Indian diplomacy but also India’s image. While it is imperative to defend India’s diplomats, it is equally important to investigate the allegations that Indian intelligence agencies have overstepped in operations in the case. The RCMP’s naming of Indian underworld gangster Lawrence Bishnoi must also be investigated. As India’s adversaries seek to draw links between allegations against Indian intelligence and national security operations in Pakistan, the UAE, Qatar, Canada and the U.S., even India’s close partners are looking askance. The U.S.’s statement, that India should cooperate with Canada, must be seen as evidence of that. India’s dual policy towards the Nijjar case, which it outrightly rejects any connection to, and the Pannun case in the U.S. — it has sent a high-level inquiry team — also raises questions. The government must prove it has nothing to hide. It must also be more transparent about how it expects to deal with this challenge, and to reports that link Canada’s allegations to India’s top leadership including National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and Home Minister Amit Shah. Above all, New Delhi must step up an international campaign to ensure accountability from Canada: to either present verifiable evidence, or to stop casting this shadow over India’s reputation and its diplomats. 
 Which of the following can be inferred from the passage about the reason behind the deteriorating India-Canada relations?
options: India’s Ministry of External Affairs accused Canada of harboring Khalistani activists.
The Canadian police suspect Indian diplomats of being involved in the killing of Hardeep Singh Nijjar.
India’s MEA accused Justin Trudeau of using the investigations for political advantage.
India and Canada have only recently developed frosty relations due to unrelated diplomatic disputes.
cpomains30.explanation:
B) The Canadian police suspect Indian diplomats of being involved in the killing of Hardeep Singh Nijjar. 
 B: The passage clearly states that the Canadian police suspect Indian diplomats are linked to the killing of Nijjar, which has contributed to the deteriorating relations. 
 A: Although India accused Canada of supporting extremists, it wasn’t presented as the primary reason for diplomatic tensions in this specific situation. 
 C: While India accused Trudeau of political motives, the inference is that the diplomatic situation is mainly due to the accusations by Canadian authorities regarding the killing of Nijjar. 
 D: The passage indicates a history of frosty relations, not a sudden deterioration due to unrelated disputes.

After a year of frosty exchanges and declining relations, India and Canada have declared diplomatic war, as India’s Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) revealed this week that the Canadian government had sought to investigate and even interrogate the Indian High Commissioner and five other diplomats, naming them “persons of interest” for the killing of Khalistani activist Hardeep Singh Nijjar. Mr. Nijjar, who was shot dead in June 2023 in British Columbia, was wanted by India. In a press conference, the Canadian police (RCMP) detailed their suspicions that the Indian diplomats were somehow involved with an Indian criminal network they believe is responsible for the killing, as well in the targeting of some in the Indian diaspora. The Canadian Ministry of Foreign Affairs has alleged political interference by India’s diplomats, something hitherto it had accused China of. India’s MEA has called the charges “preposterous”, accusing Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau of orchestrating the investigations for political gain with a pro-separatist Khalistani votebank, given his record-low ratings ahead of the 2025 general election. India also accused what it called the Canadian “regime” for providing space to “violent extremists and terrorists to ... intimidate Indian diplomats and community leaders...”, in the name of free speech. Delhi and Ottawa have each expelled six diplomats. With the reduced staff strength in the High Commissions in both capitals and an outraged India reserving the right to further action, it could well mean drastic cuts in visas and curtailed direct travel links. 
 With the die cast for worsening ties, New Delhi must consider carefully the impact of its next steps not only on Indian diplomacy but also India’s image. While it is imperative to defend India’s diplomats, it is equally important to investigate the allegations that Indian intelligence agencies have overstepped in operations in the case. The RCMP’s naming of Indian underworld gangster Lawrence Bishnoi must also be investigated. As India’s adversaries seek to draw links between allegations against Indian intelligence and national security operations in Pakistan, the UAE, Qatar, Canada and the U.S., even India’s close partners are looking askance. The U.S.’s statement, that India should cooperate with Canada, must be seen as evidence of that. India’s dual policy towards the Nijjar case, which it outrightly rejects any connection to, and the Pannun case in the U.S. — it has sent a high-level inquiry team — also raises questions. The government must prove it has nothing to hide. It must also be more transparent about how it expects to deal with this challenge, and to reports that link Canada’s allegations to India’s top leadership including National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and Home Minister Amit Shah. Above all, New Delhi must step up an international campaign to ensure accountability from Canada: to either present verifiable evidence, or to stop casting this shadow over India’s reputation and its diplomats. 
 What does the idiom “casting a shadow” mean in the context of the passage?
cpomains30.explanation:
A) Obscuring the truth 
 "Casting a shadow" means creating doubt or suspicion, which aligns with Canada casting doubts over India's reputation, as mentioned in the passage.

Comprehension: 
 I had a phobia of speaking in public. It is quite surprising given that I was good at debates during school and college. I was also a successful manager as I traversed my professional journey. I dealt with hundreds of staff since I joined the railways as a young officer.
I also interacted confidently with my peers and the seniors. However, I would break out in a sweat and lose my sleep each time I had to be on stage. I was envious of those who could spontaneously break into a joke or recite a poem. I decided to do something about it. I started preparing notes days in advance.
I would keep memorising the lines by rote till they were branded in my memory. I would even repeat them standing in front of the mirror watching intently my facial expressions. This was the best that I could do. I realised in later years that my handicap was nothing when compared to the challenges faced by many. Recently, I watched The King’s Speech, a movie on the life of King George VI, who found himself on the throne after his older brother, King Edward VIII abdicated. The film largely dealt with King George’s determination to overcome his stutter with the help of a speech therapist. I understood that the will to beat the odds comes from within.
No therapy can help an unwilling person. There are many instances of people overcoming their handicaps to pursue their dreams. We have all heard of Stephen Hawking. He was diagnosed with motor neuron disease at age 21 and was not expected to live more than a couple of years. He survived the odds but the disease paralysed him over decades. After he lost his speech, he communicated through a hand-held speech-generating device, and then through a cheek muscle. Helen Keller was an American author. Medical science was much less advanced than what we know today.
An unknown illness, when she was only 19 months old, left her permanently blind and deaf. She painstakingly learned to recognise words through hand movements. We, who are blessed, cannot even fathom the hard work that would have gone into her transformation to be the voice that she became. The famous Bharatnatyam danseuse Sudha Chandran underwent amputation of her right leg at the age of 18 due to a road accident.
Many would have lost hope and might have ended up wallowing in self-pity. The lady regained her mobility with the help of a prosthetic. She also pushed herself to accomplish the unthinkable. One need not look up to only the famous to witness these stories of human courage and conviction.
My maternal grandfather was comatose for a few months after a botched-up surgery. The doctors were not even certain about his coming out of the coma. He was paralyzed on his right side. He worked painstakingly to lead as normal a life as he could, he even developed writing skills with his left hand. Many in our country are differently abled but do not have the means to pursue their dreams.
On the other hand, we have big business houses that do not even bat an eyelid before spending more than the GDP of a small country on lavish events. We, many other individuals, and the business houses have the means to make a difference in the lives of others. Stephen Hawking said, “Concentrate on the abilities your disability doesn’t hinder and don’t dwell on the things it interferes with. Be disabled physically, not in spirit.” We need to be the spark that ignites the spirit. 
 What is the tone of the passage?
cpomains30.explanation: A)InspirationalA: This is the correct answer because the passage focuses on overcoming challenges, finding inner strength, and examples of individuals who achieved great things despite their limitations. The author's intention is to motivate readers by showcasing stories of resilience and determination.B: This is incorrect as there is no use of irony, mockery, or contemptuous language in the passage. The tone is earnest and supportive rather than sarcastic.C: This is incorrect because the passage does not express negativity or hopelessness. Instead, it highlights overcoming adversity, which is the opposite of a pessimistic viewpoint.D: This is incorrect as the author expresses strong admiration for those who have overcome challenges, making the tone highly engaged and empathetic.

options: Ignoring the fear and focusing on other tasks.
Preparing notes in advance and rehearsing extensively.
he communicated through a hand-held speech-generating device

cpomains31.word:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. 
 When a beggar appeared, / I offered him / an one rupee coin / but he did not take it.
options: but he did not take it
cpomains31.explanation:
A)An'का प्रयोग उन शब्दों से पहले होता है जो vowel sound से शुरू होते हैं, जैसे - 'an apple', 'an orange'। लेकिन यहाँ 'one' vowel ‘o’ से शुरू होता है परंतु इसकी ध्वनि 'व' (consonant sound) से शुरू होती है। अतः 'a one rupee coin' सही होगा। 
 The article 'an' is used before words that start with a vowel sound, such as 'an apple', 'an orange'. However, the word 'one' begins with the vowel letter ‘o’ but is pronounced with a consonant sound ('w'). Therefore, the correct phrase is 'a one rupee coin'.

cpomains31.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech. 
 The father said, “Ramu, try again”.
options: The father said that Ramu tries again.
The father requested Ramu to try again.
The father advised Ramu to try again.
The father told Ramu that he tried again.
cpomains31.explanation:
C)The father advised Ramu to try again 
 Reported Speech में बदलते समय, वाक्य के अर्थ और Reporting Verb पर ध्यान देना आवश्यक होता है। दिए गए वाक्य में "The father said" Reporting Verb है और "Ramu, try again" Reported Speech है। यहाँ "try again" एक सलाह (advice) या सुझाव (suggestion) दे रहा है। इसलिए Reporting Verb को "advised" में बदला गया है। 
 When converting to Reported Speech, attention must be given to the meaning of the sentence and the Reporting Verb. In the given sentence, "The father said" is the Reporting Verb, and "Ramu, try again" is the Reported Speech. Here, "try again" conveys advice or suggestion, so the Reporting Verb is appropriately changed to "advised."

Parts of a sentence/paragraph are given below. While the first and the last parts (A and F) are in the correct order, the parts in between are jumbled up. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent sentence/paragraph. 
 A. Although many people believe that video games have negative effects on children, 
 B. video games can help improve 
 C. problem-solving and strategic thinking, 
 D. through their interactive nature, 
 E. by providing challenging situations, 
 F. it is important to consider the potential benefits as well.
cpomains31.explanation:
C) D, B, C, E 
 The correct order of the parts is as follows: "Although many people believe that video games have negative effects on children, through their interactive nature, video games can help improve problem-solving and strategic thinking, by providing challenging situations, it is important to consider the potential benefits as well." This arrangement presents a coherent sentence that presents the idea of considering the positive aspects of video games, such as improving problem-solving and strategic thinking skills.

cpomains31.word:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. 
 Adult Education is a great step that must be taken by all the countries as it will__________ a lot of issues. The third world countries must especially work to make this happen so they can prosper.
cpomains31.explanation:
D)Resolve'का use होगा क्योंकि "resolve" का अर्थ है किसी समस्या या मुद्दे को हल करना। sentence में mention है कि वयस्क शिक्षा एक महान कदम है जिसे सभी देशों को उठाना चाहिए क्योंकि यह कई मुद्दों को हल करेगा। इसलिए, 'resolve' यहाँ सही है। जबकि 'contradict' का अर्थ है विरोधाभास करना, 'permeate' का अर्थ है फैल जाना या प्रवेश करना, और 'stagnate' का अर्थ है ठहराव में आना, जो इस संदर्भ में सही नहीं हैं। 
 Resolve'will be used because it means to solve or settle a problem or issue. The sentence states that adult education is a significant step that must be taken by all countries as it will address and resolve a lot of issues. Therefore, 'resolve' is the correct answer here. Whereas, 'contradict' means to oppose or deny, 'permeate' means to spread or penetrate, and 'stagnate' means to come to a standstill, none of which fit in this context.

Sentences of a paragraph are given below. While the first and the last sentences (S1 and S6) are in the correct order, the sentences in between are jumbled up. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
S1:)  The process of photosynthesis is vital for life on Earth.
A)  Chlorophyll, a pigment found in plants, captures sunlight.
B)  Oxygen is released as a byproduct, which is essential for the respiration of most organisms.
C)  The captured sunlight is used to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose.
D)   This process occurs in the chloroplasts of plant cells.
E)  The glucose is then used as an energy source for the plant to grow and reproduce.
S6:)  Ultimately, photosynthesis provides the energy and oxygen necessary for life on our planet.
cpomains31.explanation:
C) A-D-C-E-B 
 The first sentence (A) introduces chlorophyll as the pigment capturing sunlight. The next sentence (D) should mention where this process takes place - in the chloroplasts of plant cells. Following this, sentence (C) explains that sunlight is used to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose. Then, sentence (E) indicates that glucose is used as an energy source for the plant to grow and reproduce. Finally, sentence (B) explains that oxygen is released as a byproduct, which is essential for the respiration of most organisms.

 His gloomy demeanour is often criticised
cpomains31.explanation:

 Indirect Speech में बदलते समय Direct Speech में प्रयुक्त Verb और Adverbs को बदल दिया जाता है। Direct Speech में "He said" Reporting Verb है और "I am going to the party tonight" Reported Speech है। Reporting Verb "said" को बदला नहीं जाता क्योंकि यह Past Tense में है। Reported Speech में "I" को Reporting Subject "He" के अनुसार बदला गया है। "am going" (Present Continuous Tense) को Past Continuous Tense "was going" में बदला गया है। Adverb "tonight" को "that night" में बदला गया है। इस प्रकार सही उत्तर है: He said that he was going to the party that night. 
 To convert Direct Speech into Indirect Speech, the verbs and adverbs in the Reported Speech are changed according to the rules of tense and context. In the given sentence: "He said" is the Reporting Verb, and "I am going to the party tonight" is the Reported Speech. The pronoun "I" changes to "He" as per the subject of the Reporting Verb. The verb "am going" (Present Continuous Tense) changes to "was going" (Past Continuous Tense) in Indirect Speech. 
 The adverb "tonight" is changed to "that night." Thus, the correct answer is: He said that he was going to the party that night.

 Direct Speech में वाक्य को बदलते समय, reported speech को उस रूप में लिखा जाता है जैसा कि वास्तव में बोला गया था। दिए गए वाक्य में, "The traveller asked the owner if he could stay in that tavern" और "The peasant replied that he could" को Direct Speech में बदलने पर ध्यान दिया जाता है। 
 "The traveller asked the owner if he could stay in that tavern" को Direct Speech में बदलते समय, “Can I stay in this tavern?” का उपयोग किया गया है। यह सही है क्योंकि traveller ने अनुमति मांगी और Present Tense में "can" का उपयोग किया। "The peasant replied that he could" का अर्थ है कि peasant ने कहा "You can"। यह प्रतिverb सीधी और स्पष्ट है। 
 When converting to Direct Speech, the reported speech is written as it was originally spoken.  Indirect Speech में बदलने के लिए, वाक्य का Tense बदलना आवश्यक होता है। दिए गए वाक्य में Direct Speech का वाक्य "I have finished my homework" है, जो Present Perfect Tense में है। Indirect Speech में इसे Past Perfect Tense में बदल दिया जाता है। "He said" को वैसा ही रखा गया है। "I" (First Person Pronoun) को Reporting Subject "He" के अनुसार बदला गया है। "have finished" (Present Perfect) को "had finished" (Past Perfect) में बदल दिया गया है। इस प्रकार सही उत्तर है: "He said that he had finished his homework." 
 To transform a sentence into Indirect Speech, the tense of the reported speech must be changed appropriately. In the given sentence, the Direct Speech is "I have finished my homework," which is in the Present Perfect Tense. In Indirect Speech, it is changed to the Past Perfect Tense. "He said" remains unchanged. "I" (First Person Pronoun) is adjusted according to the subject of the reporting verb, which is "He." "have finished" (Present Perfect) is transformed into "had finished" (Past Perfect). Thus, the correct answer is: "He said that he had finished his homework."

Mohan said that he would go as soon as it is possible.
Mohan said that he will go as soon as it was possible.
Mohan said that he will go as soon as it is possible.
cpomains31.explanation:
A)Mohan said that he would go as soon as it was possible. 
 Reported Speech में वाक्य बदलते समय, Direct Speech के Verb को Indirect Speech के अनुसार बदल दिया जाता है। दिए गए वाक्य में, Direct Speech में "shall" है, जो Reported Speech में "would" में बदल जाएगा। "as soon as it is possible" में, "is" को Past Tense में बदलकर "was" किया जाएगा, क्योंकि Reporting Verb "said" Past Tense में है। इसलिए सही विकल्प A है: "Mohan said that he would go as soon as it was possible।" 
 When converting a sentence into Reported Speech, the verb in Direct Speech is changed to its corresponding form in Indirect Speech. In the given sentence, "shall" in Direct Speech changes to "would" in Reported Speech. The phrase "as soon as it is possible" requires "is" to be converted to "was" since the Reporting Verb "said" is in the past tense. 
 Hence, the correct option is A: Mohan said that he would go as soon as it was possible.

 'Branches'will be used because it refers to the limbs or parts of a tree that can break off during a heavy rain or storm.  Appropriate'will be used because it means "suitable" or "exact," which fits the context that farmers grow crops suitable for the season. The sentence mentions that farmers begin their fieldwork and grow crops using the natural water supply, making 'appropriate' the correct word. 
 'Inadequate' means "insufficient," which does not make sense here as it implies the crops are insufficient. 'Incompatible' means "not suitable" or "not matching," which does not fit the context of crops grown by farmers. 'Manipulating' means "to handle something cleverly or skillfully," which is not relevant to the context of growing crops.

 Direct Speechमें वाक्य को Active Voice में लिखा जाता है औरIndirect Speechसे इसे वापस बदलते समय वाक्य का मूल संदर्भ, tense, और शब्दावली का ध्यान रखना पड़ता है। यहां"He said" reporting verb है, और"it would be fun if I could join" reported speech है। said" का प्रयोग बिना किसी reporting verb change के direct speech में किया गया है। Indirect Speech में"would" का प्रयोग future possibility या conditional sentence के लिए होता है। Direct Speech में इसे"will" और"can" के रूप में परिवर्तित किया जाता है, क्योंकि यह संभावना(possibility) और वर्तमान समय के लिए उपयुक्त है। "I" को"you" में बदला जाता है, क्योंकि reporting का दृष्टिकोण बदल गया है। 
 To convert a sentence from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech, the original context, tense, and pronouns must be adjusted appropriately. The reporting verb "said" remains unchanged as there is no need to modify it while converting to direct speech. In indirect speech, "would" indicates a future possibility or a conditional statement. In direct speech, "would" is reverted to "will" (present/future tense) and "could" to "can," as it represents a possibility in the present or near future. The pronoun "I" from the indirect speech changes to "you" in direct speech, reflecting the perspective of the person being addressed.

Comprehension: 
 In the scorching summer of 1880, a healthy baby girl was born in the quiet town of Tuscumbia, Alabama. Her parents, overjoyed with her arrival, named her Helen Keller. She quickly became the light of their lives. However, tragedy struck when little Helen fell gravely ill. Day after day, her fever remained alarmingly high, and despite every effort her family made, no improvement followed. Despair crept into the household, as even the doctors said with sorrow, “There is nothing more we can do. The baby may not survive.” 
 But Helen defied the odds—she lived. Yet something had changed. As the days passed, her mother began to notice disturbing signs. “Something is very wrong,” she whispered anxiously. After consulting specialists, the devastating truth emerged: Helen had lost both her sight and hearing. The once-healthy baby was now locked in a world of silence and darkness. 
 As Helen grew into a young child, her parents' sympathy for her condition deepened, and they often gave in to her every whim. Helen would cling to her mother, weeping in frustration, while her father, unable to bear her distress, would plead, “Give the poor child whatever she wants.” 
 Though deprived of her senses, Helen was an intelligent little girl. Unfortunately, many doubted her ability to learn or develop, believing her disabilities had left her mind as unreachable as her senses. But her mother fiercely disagreed. “Helen is exceptionally smart,” she insisted. “The problem lies in how we can reach her. She is trapped within herself, unable to communicate.” 
 As Helen grew older, her frustration manifested in wild and uncontrollable behavior. She refused to be restrained, lashing out at her family and even rejecting basic grooming. Combing her hair became an impossible task as Helen rebelled against any form of touch or care. The once-bright child had become lost in a world of chaos and confusion, her soul yearning for connection yet unable to find a way to express it. 
 Desperate, her parents knew they needed a miracle—someone who could unlock the brilliance they believed still existed within Helen. And thus, the long and arduous journey to find a teacher who could bridge the gap between Helen's isolated world and the outside reality began.

Comprehension:
People often question whether anybody can work sincerely and efficiently without desire. Sincerity becomes natural, and efficiency peaks when actions are no longer motivated by desires. Desire makes the mind cling to future gain or loss instead of the present task. It accompanies expectation, anxiety, and fear and affects attention and performance. We are born with an insufficiency that makes us look for happiness externally. We are born with the delusion that something from the world will fulfil that lack and make us happy. Has anybody ever become permanently happy by gaining anything from the world – money, power, companionship, fame, or appreciation? Even the most overwhelming happiness lasts until the mind picks up some other lack or a fear of losing what we have gained. It is not the fulfilment of our desires that makes us happy. It is the elimination of desires that truly makes us happy.
When a desire is fulfilled, the mind becomes ‘desireless’ for a while. It remains contented and peaceful until another desire for gaining something or fear of losing something agitates it again. It is the undisturbed state of the mind that makes us happy. It reveals for a while the placid joy that is always there within as a natural characteristic of our inmost identity, the Self. It is like seeing the bottom of the lake clearly when there are no waves or ripples. That is why we experience unprecedented joy or bliss in meditation, when the whole world is forgotten, and the mind is absorbed in its Source.
The day we realise that joy comes from within, it is a natural property of our Self; we understand that desires make us unhappy because they take us away from the Self. If joy lies within, why should we chase external objects that give us pleasure? If we do not expect happiness from the objective result of our work, what will be the motivation for work? The motivation for work will be just the objective result of the action, and not gaining happiness from the desired objective result. Without desire, our mind will be naturally placid and fulfilled. We shall do whatever the circumstances need and what is within our capacity. No more shall we work expecting happiness. We will do whatever is to be done as an expression of joy, and such desireless performance can produce the best objective results.
Several activities are constantly going on in the universe. Earth revolves around the Sun, and the Moon revolves around Earth. Rivers flow. Plants grow. Flowers blossom – each with its own colour and beauty. Nowhere is there desire. When desires are diminished, we blossom like flowers in our natural svabhava, nature, spreading joy.
According to the passage, why does desire negatively impact sincerity and efficiency in work?
options: Because desire makes the mind focus on future gain or loss rather than the present task.
Because desire encourages hard work and dedication.
Because desire eliminates expectations and anxiety.
Because desire enhances attention and performance.
cpomains31.explanation:
A) Because desire makes the mind focus on future gain or loss rather than the present task. 
 A is correct because the passage states that desire "makes the mind cling to future gain or loss instead of the present task," which negatively affects sincerity and efficiency.B is incorrect because while desire might motivate action, the passage emphasizes that it detracts from sincerity and efficiency by focusing on future outcomes, not enhancing dedication.C is incorrect because the passage mentions that desire "accompanies expectation, anxiety, and fear," so it does not eliminate them.D is incorrect because desire affects attention and performance negatively by causing anxiety and fear, not enhancing them.

Comprehension:
People often question whether anybody can work sincerely and efficiently without desire. Sincerity becomes natural, and efficiency peaks when actions are no longer motivated by desires. Desire makes the mind cling to future gain or loss instead of the present task. It accompanies expectation, anxiety, and fear and affects attention and performance. We are born with an insufficiency that makes us look for happiness externally. We are born with the delusion that something from the world will fulfil that lack and make us happy. Has anybody ever become permanently happy by gaining anything from the world – money, power, companionship, fame, or appreciation? Even the most overwhelming happiness lasts until the mind picks up some other lack or a fear of losing what we have gained. It is not the fulfilment of our desires that makes us happy. It is the elimination of desires that truly makes us happy.
When a desire is fulfilled, the mind becomes ‘desireless’ for a while. It remains contented and peaceful until another desire for gaining something or fear of losing something agitates it again. It is the undisturbed state of the mind that makes us happy. It reveals for a while the placid joy that is always there within as a natural characteristic of our inmost identity, the Self. It is like seeing the bottom of the lake clearly when there are no waves or ripples. That is why we experience unprecedented joy or bliss in meditation, when the whole world is forgotten, and the mind is absorbed in its Source.
The day we realise that joy comes from within, it is a natural property of our Self; we understand that desires make us unhappy because they take us away from the Self. If joy lies within, why should we chase external objects that give us pleasure? If we do not expect happiness from the objective result of our work, what will be the motivation for work? The motivation for work will be just the objective result of the action, and not gaining happiness from the desired objective result. Without desire, our mind will be naturally placid and fulfilled. We shall do whatever the circumstances need and what is within our capacity. No more shall we work expecting happiness. We will do whatever is to be done as an expression of joy, and such desireless performance can produce the best objective results.

Flowers blossom – each with its own colour and beauty. Nowhere is there desire. When desires are diminished, we blossom like flowers in our natural svabhava, nature, spreading joy.

A silent forest untouched by wind.

Comprehension: 
 The passing of Ratan Tata, one of India’s most influential and revered business leaders, marks the end of an era for Indian industry and philanthropy. A visionary who transformed the Tata Group into a global powerhouse, Ratan Tata not only redefined Indian business practices but also set new standards for ethical leadership and corporate responsibility. His demise has left an indelible void in the Indian business landscape and his contributions will continue to shape India’s socio-economic fabric for generations to come. Ratan Tata’s leadership of the Tata Group from 1991 to 2012 is widely recognised as a period of extraordinary innovation and growth. He was instrumental in leading the conglomerate’s diversification, moving it beyond its traditional industries like steel and textiles into sectors such as information technology, automotive, telecommunications and hospitality. Under his stewardship, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) became a global leader in IT services. Tata Motors expanded its reach with the acquisitions of British automotive giants Jaguar and Land Rover in 2008. Tata’s vision of making India a global player was rooted in a deep sense of nationalism, combined with a keen awareness of global business trends. Ratan Tata’s most cherished moment came when Tata Motors launched the Nano in 2008 despite all odds. Though the Nano did not achieve commercial success, the boldness of the vision highlighted Tata’s commitment to solving Indian problems with innovative solutions and realising the aspirations of Indian middle class. 
 Known for his humility and discretion, he always emphasised that businesses should serve society at large. “We have to touch the lives of people in ways that matter,” Tata often said. Nearly two-thirds of Tata Group’s profits are directed to social work through Tata Trusts, a remarkable legacy in Indian philanthropy. The Tata Trusts, under his guidance, funded several initiatives in healthcare, education and rural development. Tata maintained a reputation for being soft-spoken and modest, rarely allowing his personal life to take centre stage in the public eye. His leadership during the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks, where the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel was one of the primary targets, showed his resilience. Tata visited the families of affected staff members, providing support and ensuring that the hotel was rebuilt, symbolising the spirit of survival and recovery. Despite numerous achievements, Tata faced failures with grace. His decisions, such as the Nano, received criticism, but he handled setbacks with the   dignity that defined him. His resilience and forward-thinking approach is his legacy that would inspire many. Ratan Tata’s life was not just about business. His love for architecture, aviation and cars was well known. Despite his status as one of India’s richest individuals, he led a simple life, often seen without an entourage, and known for driving himself. With Ratan Tata’s passing, India has lost a visionary and a kind hearted leader who would be remembered for his achievements and resilience. Rest in peace! 
 What is the tone of the passage?
cpomains31.explanation:
B) Reflective and appreciative 
 The passage reflects on Ratan Tata's life and contributions with admiration and respect, showcasing a reflective and appreciative tone. 
 A is incorrect because the passage does not criticize or express pessimism about Ratan Tata's life or actions. 
 C is incorrect because the passage maintains a serious and respectful tone, without humor or sarcasm. 
 D is incorrect because the passage is emotionally engaged, not indifferent or merely objective.

Tata’s vision of making India a global player was rooted in a deep sense of nationalism, combined with a keen awareness of global business trends. Ratan Tata’s most cherished moment came when Tata Motors launched the Nano in 2008 despite all odds. Though the Nano did not achieve commercial success, the boldness of the vision highlighted Tata’s commitment to solving Indian problems with innovative solutions and realising the aspirations of Indian middle class. 
 Known for his humility and discretion, he always emphasised that businesses should serve society at large. “We have to touch the lives of people in ways that matter,” Tata often said. Nearly two-thirds of Tata Group’s profits are directed to social work through Tata Trusts, a remarkable legacy in Indian philanthropy. The Tata Trusts, under his guidance, funded several initiatives in healthcare, education and rural development. Tata maintained a reputation for being soft-spoken and modest, rarely allowing his personal life to take centre stage in the public eye. His leadership during the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks, where the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel was one of the primary targets, showed his resilience. Tata visited the families of affected staff members, providing support and ensuring that the hotel was rebuilt, symbolising the spirit of survival and recovery. Despite numerous achievements, Tata faced failures with grace. His decisions, such as the Nano, received criticism, but he handled setbacks with the   dignity that defined him. His resilience and forward-thinking approach is his legacy that would inspire many. Ratan Tata’s life was not just about business. His love for architecture, aviation and cars was well known. Despite his status as one of India’s richest individuals, he led a simple life, often seen without an entourage, and known for driving himself. A)'Enough'का use होगा क्योंकि "enough" का अर्थ होता है पर्याप्त या किसी चीज़ के लिए योग्य। वाक्य में कहा गया है कि वह नौकरी के लिए अच्छा है, और 'enough' इस संदर्भ में सही है क्योंकि यह व्यक्ति की योग्यता को स्पष्ट करता है। जबकि 'Rather' का अर्थ है "कुछ हद तक" या "काफी," 'Altogether' का अर्थ है "पूरी तरह से" और 'Partly' का अर्थ है "आंशिक रूप से," जो इस वाक्य के लिए उपयुक्त नहीं हैं। 
 'Enough' will be used because it means sufficient or adequate for something. The sentence conveys that he is good enough for the job, making 'enough' the correct choice as it emphasizes his suitability. Whereas, 'Rather' means "to some extent" or "quite," 'Altogether' means "completely," and 'Partly' means "to some degree," none of which fit this context.

Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. 
 Malathi loves Reena
options: Reena is being loved by Malathi.
Reena was being loved by Malathi.
cpomains32.explanation:
C)Reena is loved by Malathi. 
 Active से Passive Voice में बदलने के लिए, Active वाक्य का Object Passive वाक्य का Subject बन जाता है। Verb को Active से Passive में बदलते समय सही Tense का प्रयोग किया जाता है। Active वाक्य में "Malathi" Subject है, "loves" Verb (Simple Present) है और "Reena" Object है। Passive में बदलने पर Object "Reena" Subject बन गया है, Verb को "is loved" (Simple Present Passive) में बदला गया है और "by Malathi" के रूप में प्रयोग किया गया है। 
 To change a sentence from Active to Passive Voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence. The verb is transformed from the active form to the passive form, ensuring correct tense usage. In this case, "Malathi" (Subject), "loves" (Verb in Simple Present), and "Reena" (Object) from the active voice have been transformed into "Reena" (Subject), "is loved" (Passive Verb in Simple Present), and "by Malathi".

Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. 
 She asked me why I was not eating
options: She said, “Why is he not eating?”
She said, “Why am I not eating?”
She said, “Why are you not eating?”
cpomains32.explanation:
D)She said, “Why are you not eating?” 
 Direct Speech में वाक्य को बदलते समय, Reported Speech (जो कहा गया है) को उसके मूल स्वरूप में लिखा जाता है। वाक्य "She asked me why I was not eating" में Indirect Speech दी गई है। इसमें "was not eating" (Past Continuous Tense) का प्रयोग किया गया है। इसे Direct Speech में बदलते समय, वाक्य को Present Continuous Tense में लिखा जाएगा क्योंकि प्रश्न सीधे रूप में पूछा गया है। "She asked me" को "She said" में बदल दिया गया है और "you" का प्रयोग प्रश्नकर्ता (me) के लिए किया गया है। इस प्रक्रिया के अनुसार, वाक्य "She said, 'Why are you not eating?'" सही रूप है। 
 When converting a sentence to Direct Speech, the reported speech (what is said) is written in its original form. In the given sentence "She asked me why I was not eating," the Indirect Speech uses "was not eating" (Past Continuous Tense). While converting to Direct Speech, the sentence is written in Present Continuous Tense because the question is asked directly. The phrase "She asked me" is replaced with "She said," and "you" is used for the second person (me). Thus, the correct sentence is "She said, 'Why are you not eating?'".

cpomains32.word:
Select the option that correctly expresses the following sentence in direct speech. 
 She told me that she had already finished the project.
options: She told me, “He had already finished the project.”
She said to me, “I have already finished the project.”
She said, “She will have finished the project.”
She said to her, “I already finished the project
cpomains32.explanation:
B)She said to me, “I have already finished the project.” 
 Direct से Indirect Speech में बदलने के लिए वाक्य के Tense और Pronouns को बदलने का नियम लागू होता है। यह वाक्य Indirect Speech में है:"She told me that she had already finished the project."Indirect Speech में "had already finished" (Past Perfect) का use किया गया है। Direct Speech में इसका मूल स्वरूप "have already finished" (Present Perfect) होगा क्योंकि Reporting Verb "told" का समय Reporting Clause के Present से जुड़ा हुआ है।Indirect Speech में "she" का use किया गया है। Direct Speech में यह "I" में बदल जाएगा, क्योंकि First-Person Pronoun हमेशा Speaker (She) को दर्शाता हैReporting Verb "told me" Direct Speech में "said to me" में बदलेगा। 
 To convert from Indirect to Direct Speech, rules for transforming Tense and Pronouns are applied. The given sentence in Indirect Speech is:"She told me that she had already finished the project. "In Indirect Speech, "had already finished" (Past Perfect) is used. In Direct Speech, it reverts to its original form, "have already finished" (Present Perfect), as the reporting verb "told" implies a connection to the time of speaking. In Indirect Speech, "she" is used. In Direct Speech, it changes to "I," as it represents the first-person perspective of the speaker (She). The reporting verb "told me" changes to "said to me" in Direct Speech.

 Reported Speech में बदलने के लिए प्रक्रिया समझाते हुए: जब Direct Speech को Indirect Speech (Reported Speech) में बदलते हैं, तो Reporting Verb और Reported Speech दोनों में परिवर्तन होता है। Reporting Verb के Tense के आधार पर Reported Speech का Tense बदला जाता है। इस वाक्य में "Koushik said to Tarun" Reporting Clause है और "You are a good cricketer" Reported Speech है। Reporting Verb "said to" को Indirect Speech में "told" में बदल दिया गया। "You" (Second Person Pronoun) को Reporting Verb के Object "Tarun" के अनुसार "he" में बदल दिया गया। Present Tense "are" को Past Tense "was" में बदल दिया गया क्योंकि Reporting Verb Past Tense में है। Reported Speech को "that" का use करके Indirect Speech में बदला गया। 
 When converting Direct Speech into Indirect Speech (Reported Speech), both the Reporting Verb and the Reported Speech undergo modifications. The tense of the Reported Speech changes based on the tense of the Reporting Verb. In this case, "Koushik said to Tarun" is the Reporting Clause, and "You are a good cricketer" is the Reported Speech. The Reporting Verb "said to" is changed to "told" in Indirect Speech. "You" (Second Person Pronoun) is replaced with "he" according to the Object of the Reporting Verb, "Tarun." The Present Tense "are" is changed to Past Tense "was" because the Reporting Verb is in the Past Tense. 
 The Reported Speech is connected with the help of "that" in Indirect Speech.

 He said to his soldiers, “Take this bird away. Its gilded cage reminds me of my father whom I imprisoned.”

 Above'will be used because it correctly fits the idiomatic expression "over and above," which means "in addition to" or "besides."  B:This sentence explains why July (from sentence C) is significant, providing context for the anxiety. It describes the activities done during this time. The use of "It is the season" acts as a connector, expanding on the reason for the anxiety introduced in sentence C 
 D:This sentence further builds upon the anxiety theme, suggesting that even the most careful individuals are worried until their tax processes are complete. The use of "Even" emphasizes the intensity of the sentiment introduced in sentences C and B
