cpomains32.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. 
 Srikar had been promised good support by Mahitha.
options: Mahitha will have promised Srikar good support.
Mahitha had promised good support to Srikar.
Mahitha promises good support to Srikar.
Mahitha has promised Srikar good support
cpomains32.explanation:
B)Mahitha had promised good support to Srikar 
 Active Voice से Passive Voice में बदलने के लिए Object और Subject की अदला-बदली होती है और Verb को Passive Form में परिवर्तित किया जाता है। Passive वाक्य "Srikar had been promised good support by Mahitha" है। Passive वाक्य में "Srikar" (Object) को Active वाक्य में Subject बनाया जाएगा। 
 Passive वाक्य का Verb "had been promised" (Past Perfect Passive) है। इसे Active Voice में "had promised" (Past Perfect Active) में बदला जाएगा। "by Mahitha" को Active Voice में Subject के रूप में रखा जाएगा। Active वाक्य बनेगा: "Mahitha had promised good support to Srikar." 
 To change a sentence from Passive to Active Voice, the subject and object swap places, and the verb is converted from passive to active form. The Passive sentence is: "Srikar had been promised good support by Mahitha." In the Passive sentence, "Srikar" (Object) becomes the Subject in the Active sentence. The Passive verb "had been promised" (Past Perfect Passive) is converted to "had promised" (Past Perfect Active). "by Mahitha" is used as the Subject in the Active voice. The Active sentence is: "Mahitha had promised good support to Srikar."

Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. 
 He asked me affectionately what he could do for me.
options: He said to me, “What should be done for you?”

C)He said to me, “What can I do for you, dear?” 
 यह वाक्य Indirect Speech में है। इसे Direct Speech में बदलने के लिए निम्नलिखित चरणों का पालन किया जाता है: Indirect वाक्य में "asked me affectionately" को Direct Speech में बदलते समय "said to me, '...' dear" में बदला गया। "what he could do for me" को Direct Speech में बदलते समय, "he" को "I" और "could" को "can" में बदला गया क्योंकि यह अनुरूपता और वाक्य संरचना के अनुसार है। वाक्य में affectionately (स्नेहपूर्वक) का संकेत "dear" से किया गया है। 
 This sentence is in Indirect Speech and needs to be transformed into Direct Speech. The steps are as follows: The phrase "asked me affectionately" in Indirect Speech becomes "said to me, '...' dear" in Direct Speech. The clause "what he could do for me" is transformed into "What can I do for you" in Direct Speech. The pronoun "he" changes to "I," and "could" changes to "can" to maintain grammatical correctness and context. The affectionate tone is retained with the use of "dear" in the Direct Speech.

cpomains32.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech. 
 Jatin said, “I was at home yesterday
options: Jatin said he was at home the day before.
Jatin said that he had been at home the day before.

Jatin said he was at home.
cpomains32.explanation:
B)Jatin said that he had been at home the day before 
 Indirect Speech में वाक्य बदलने के लिए Reported Speech (जो Jatin ने कहा) के Tense को Reported Verb के आधार पर बदला जाता है।Direct SpeechमेंReported Verb "said"है,जोPast Tense में है। Direct Speech का वाक्य है: "I was at home yesterday"। इसमें "was" (Past Tense) है और "yesterday" एक समय-संकेतक (Time Indicator) है। Indirect Speech में Time Indicator बदलता है:"yesterday" → "the day before" "was" (Past Tense) को Indirect Speech में Past Perfect "had been" में बदल दिया जाता है क्योंकि Reported Verb (said) Past Tense में है। 
 To convert a sentence into Indirect Speech, the tense of the Reported Speech is adjusted based on the Reported Verb. In the given Direct Speech, the Reported Verb is "said," which is in the Past Tense. The Direct Speech sentence is: "I was at home yesterday" where "was" is in the Past Tense and "yesterday" is a time indicator. In Indirect Speech: The time indicator changes: "yesterday" → "the day before." The verb "was" (Past Tense) is changed to "had been" (Past Perfect) because the Reported Verb "said" is in the Past Tense.

 To change Passive to Active Voice: In the passive sentence "Devotional songs are sung superbly by Sastri," the subject of the passive sentence "Devotional songs" becomes the object of the active sentence. The verb "are sung" in Present Simple Passive changes to "sings" in Present Simple Active. The agent "by Sastri" becomes the subject "Sastri" in the active sentence. Hence, the active sentence becomes "Sastri sings devotional songs superbly."

 Passive से Active Voice में बदलने के लिए: Passive वाक्य का Subject Active वाक्य का Object बन जाता है और Verb को Passive से Active में बदलते समय सही Tense का प्रयोग किया जाता है। 
 Given Sentence (Passive): The couple was trolled by everyone. 
 Passive वाक्य में "The couple" Subject है। "was trolled" Verb है (Past Simple Passive)। "by everyone" Agent है 
 Active वाक्य में बदलने पर: Passive वाक्य का Agent ("by everyone") Active वाक्य का Subject बन गया है। Verb "was trolled" को Past Simple Active "trolled" में बदला गया है। Passive वाक्य का Subject ("The couple") Active वाक्य का Object बन गया है। 
 To change from Passive to Active Voice: The object of the passive sentence becomes the subject of the active sentence. The verb is transformed from passive to active form while maintaining the tense. Given Sentence (Passive): The couple was trolled by everyone. In this sentence, "The couple" is the subject, "was trolled" is the verb in Past Simple Passive, and "by everyone" is the agent. 
 Active Sentence Conversion: The agent ("everyone") becomes the subject. The verb "was trolled" (Past Simple Passive) changes to "trolled" (Past Simple Active). The subject of the passive voice ("The couple") becomes the object in the active voice.

cpomains32.word:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in direct speech. 
 He told me that he would have finished the project by the following day
options: I have finished the project by tomorrow,” he said to me.
“I will have finished the project by tomorrow,” he said to me.
“I will finish the project by the next day,” he said to me.
“I would finish the project,” he said to me tomorrow
cpomains32.explanation:
B) “I will have finished the project by tomorrow,” he said to me. 
 Direct Speech में वाक्य को बदलते समय, Reported Speech का Original रूप बहाल किया जाता है। दिए गए वाक्य में, Indirect Speech में "he told me that he would have finished the project by the following day" दिया गया है। Reported Speech में 'he would have finished' Future Perfect Tense को Indirect में दर्शाता है। Future Perfect Tense को Direct Speech में बदलते समय, इसे "will have finished" में परिवर्तित किया जाता है। "By the following day" को Direct Speech में "by tomorrow" के रूप में लिखा जाता है। इसलिए, सही विकल्प होगा: "I will have finished the project by tomorrow," he said to me. 
 When converting a sentence from Indirect to Direct Speech, the original form of the Reported Speech is restored. In the given sentence, the Indirect Speech is "he told me that he would have finished the project by the following day." In the Indirect Speech, "he would have finished" represents the Future Perfect Tense. While converting to Direct Speech, it becomes "will have finished." "By the following day" in Indirect Speech changes to "by tomorrow" in Direct Speech. Thus, the correct option is: "I will have finished the project by tomorrow," he said to me.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. 
 You can tell yourself that you would be willing to lose everything you have in order to get something you want: all of those things you’re willing to lose are what make you___________.

A)'Recognisable'का use किया जाएगा क्योंकि यह दर्शाता है कि जो चीज़ें आपको पहचानने योग्य बनाती हैं, वे वे हैं जिन्हें आप खोने के लिए तैयार हैं। वाक्य का संदर्भ यह है कि जो चीज़ें आप खोने के लिए तैयार हैं, वे आपकी पहचान को परिभाषित करती हैं। अन्य विकल्प इस संदर्भ में सही नहीं बैठते। 'Unfortunately' का अर्थ है "दुर्भाग्य से," जो वाक्य के भाव से मेल नहीं खाता। 'Pessimist' का अर्थ है "निराशावादी व्यक्ति," लेकिन वाक्य में किसी व्यक्ति के दृष्टिकोण का संदर्भ नहीं है। 'Distract' का अर्थ है "ध्यान भटकाना," जो इस संदर्भ में वाक्य के भाव और अर्थ को नहीं दर्शाता। 
 Recognisable'will be used because it refers to the qualities or things that make you identifiable, which is the core idea of the sentence. The sentence discusses the willingness to lose things that define or make you recognisable. 'Unfortunately' means "by bad luck," which doesn’t fit the context of identity or recognition. 'Pessimist' refers to someone with a negative outlook, but the sentence does not discuss personal perspectives. 'Distract' means "to divert attention," which is unrelated to the sentence's focus on identity or recognition.

 To convert from Indirect to Direct Speech, the Reporting Verb "said" is paired with the Reporting Speech in quotation marks. The modal verb "could" is reverted to "can," as it reflects the present form in Direct Speech. The correct Direct Speech sentence is "She said, 'I can bake cookies.'"

Select the most appropriate form and tense of the bracketed verb in the following sentence to fill in the blank. 
 I’m busy today. I’d rather we ________ (has) the meeting tomorrow.
cpomains32.explanation:
D)Had'का use होगा क्योंकि 'I'd rather' (I would rather) के बाद एक hypothetical या imaginary situation व्यक्त करने के लिए past tense का use होता है। यह वाक्य एक सुझाव या प्राथमिकता को व्यक्त करता है। वाक्य का अर्थ है "मैं आज व्यस्त हूँ। मैं चाहूँगा कि हमारी बैठक कल हो।" इस संदर्भ में, 'had' सही विकल्प है। 'Had been' का अर्थ है "था" या "हो चुका था," जो वाक्य के वर्तमान संदर्भ में फिट नहीं होता। 'Has been' वर्तमान परिपूर्ण काल (present perfect tense) में है, जो यहां उपयुक्त नहीं है। 'Has' present tense का एक रूप है, लेकिन यह 'I'd rather' के साथ सही नहीं बैठता। 
 Had'will be used because 'I'd rather' (I would rather) is followed by a hypothetical or imaginary situation, and the past tense is used to express such preferences. The sentence implies a suggestion or preference: "I’m busy today. I’d rather we had the meeting tomorrow." In this context, 'had' is the correct option. 'Had been' refers to a state in the past or something that had already occurred, which does not fit the current context. 
 'Has been' is in the present perfect tense, which is not suitable here. 'Has' is a present tense form, but it does not fit grammatically with 'I'd rather

 'Apparent'will be used because it means "clear" or "easily understood." The sentence mentions that the train stopped suddenly without any clear reason, which caused panic among passengers. cpomains32.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. 
 The interviewers were asking difficult questions.
options: Difficult questions were being asked by the interviewers.
Difficult questions are being asked by the interviewers.
Difficult questions are asked by the interviewers.
Difficult questions were asked by the interviewers.
cpomains32.explanation:
A)Difficult questions were being asked by the interviewers 
 Active से Passive Voice में बदलने के लिए, Active वाक्य का Object Passive वाक्य का Subject बन जाता है। Verb को Active से Passive में बदलते समय सही Tense का प्रयोग किया जाता है। 
 Active वाक्य में: 
 Subject: "The interviewers" 
 Verb: "were asking" (Past Continuous) 
 Object: "difficult questions" 
 Passive में बदलने पर: Object "difficult questions" को Subject बनाया गया। Verb "were asking" को Passive में "were being asked" में बदला गया। Agent "by the interviewers" के रूप में वाक्य में जोड़ा गया। Passive Sentence: "Difficult questions were being asked by the interviewers." 
 To change a sentence from Active to Passive Voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence. The verb is transformed from the active form to the passive form, ensuring correct tense usage. 
 In the active sentence: 
 Subject: "The interviewers" 
 Verb: "were asking" (Past Continuous) 
 Object: "difficult questions" 
 In the passive transformation: The object "difficult questions" becomes the subject. 
 The verb "were asking" is transformed into "were being asked" (Passive in Past Continuous). 
 The agent "by the interviewers" is added. Passive Sentence: "Difficult questions were being asked by the interviewers."

 P)  The popular greetings “Happy Holidays” during festive seasons seem to stem from the idea that holiday and happiness go together.

 S)  The weekends hold high hopes of carefree holidaying, reminding us of Charles Lamb’s observation that the prospect of a Sunday is more pleasurable than the “Sabbath recreations” themselves. A holiday is sweet, but the prospect of a holiday is sweeter. 
 S4)  It has a charm of its own to one and all: the child in the primary class, the teenager at school or college, the quill-driver in a private or public office, the man of brawn who wields the pickaxe, and the mechanic who turns the lathe, all welcome a holiday with the same spirit of joy.
cpomains32.explanation:
C) P and S 
 S1is about the origin and evolution of the word "holiday." 
 Prelates to this by expanding on the connection between holidays and happiness. 
 S2should ideally continue the theme by building on the concept of holidays and their cultural or emotional significance. 
 Sdoes just that by exploring the anticipation and joy people feel leading up to a holiday. 
 Qis about a specific event in Noida, and it doesn't seem to connect with the theme of the paragraph. 
 R,similarly, refers to a specific event about traffic jams during holidays, but it doesn't delve into the emotional or cultural significance of holidays, which is the thread running through S1. 
 S4talks about the universal appeal and joy of holidays to different groups of people, which connects smoothly with S and its exploration of the joy of anticipation.

cpomains32.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech. 
 "I am playing the keyboard," she explained.
options: She explained that she is playing the keyboard.
She said that she is playing the keyboard.
She explained that she was playing the keyboard.
She said that she had been playing the keyboard
cpomains32.explanation:
C)She explained that she was playing the keyboard 
 Direct से Indirect Speech में बदलने के लिए, Reporting Verb और Reported Speech के Tense का ध्यान रखना आवश्यक है। यहाँ Reporting Verb "explained" (Past Tense) में है, इसलिए Reported Speech का Tense बदलकर Past में किया जाएगा। वाक्य "I am playing the keyboard" (Direct Speech) में "am playing" (Present Continuous) है। इसे Indirect Speech में बदलते समय "was playing" (Past Continuous) में बदला गया है। "She" (Subject) को Reporting Speech के अनुरूप रखा गया है, और Personal Pronoun "I" को Reporting Speaker के हिसाब से "she" में बदल दिया गया है। 
 To convert a sentence from Direct to Indirect Speech, the tense of the Reported Speech is adjusted based on the Reporting Verb. Here, the Reporting Verb "explained" is in the Past Tense, so the tense of the Reported Speech is shifted to the past. The sentence "I am playing the keyboard" (Direct Speech) has "am playing" in the Present Continuous tense. When converted to Indirect Speech, it becomes "was playing" in the Past Continuous tense. The Subject "She" remains consistent with the Reporting Speech, and the Pronoun "I" is changed to "she" to align with the speaker.

cpomains32.word:
Select the correct alternative from the given options that correctly changes the form of narration in the given sentence. 
 The Headmistress said, “What a performance!”
options: The Headmistress exclaimed that it was a great performance.
The Headmistress praised what a great performance.

The Headmistress said that what a performance
cpomains32.explanation:
A)The Headmistress exclaimed that it was a great performance 
 Direct से Indirect Speech में बदलने के लिए: Direct Speech में "The Headmistress said, 'What a performance!'" में "said" Reporting Verb है और "What a performance!" Reported Speech है। यह एक exclamatory sentence है, जिसमें भाव व्यक्त किया गया है। Indirect Speech में बदलते समय Reporting Verb "said" को "exclaimed" में बदल दिया गया है क्योंकि यह एक भावुक expression है। Reported Speech को Indirect में बदलते समय "What a performance!" को "it was a great performance" में बदला गया है। "What" का use भाव को व्यक्त करने के लिए किया गया था, जो Indirect Speech में "a great" के रूप में परिवर्तित होता है 
 To change Direct Speech to Indirect Speech: In the given sentence, "The Headmistress said, 'What a performance!'", "said" is the Reporting Verb, and "What a performance!" is the Reported Speech. Since this is an exclamatory sentence expressing emotion, the Reporting Verb "said" is changed to "exclaimed." The Reported Speech, "What a performance!" is transformed into "it was a great performance" in Indirect Speech. The exclamation "What" used to express admiration is replaced by "a great" to appropriately convey the meaning in Indirect Speech.

 When converting from Direct to Indirect Speech, we need to pay attention to the tense of the Reporting Verb and the Reported Speech. The Reporting Verb "said" is in the Past Tense. 
 The Reported Speech "I have finished my work" is in Present Perfect Tense. If the Reporting Verb is in the Past Tense, the Reported Speech tense shifts one step back: Present Perfect (have finished) changes to Past Perfect (had finished). The pronoun "I" changes to "she" according to the Reporting Subject ("She").

B)The'का use होगा क्योंकि "Himalayas" एक proper noun है जो एक विशिष्ट और अद्वितीय पर्वत श्रृंखला को संदर्भित करता है। 'The' का उपयोग ऐसे nouns के पहले होता है जो विशिष्टता (specificity) को दर्शाते हैं। यहाँ 'Himalayas' के पहले 'The' लगाना आवश्यक है ताकि यह स्पष्ट हो सके कि यह एक विशेष स्थान का उल्लेख कर रहा है। 'An' का उपयोग singular nouns के साथ होता है जो vowel sound से शुरू होते हैं, और "Himalayas" plural है, इसलिए यह गलत है। 'No article' (किसी article का उपयोग न करना) भी गलत है क्योंकि proper nouns जैसे "Himalayas" के लिए definite article ('The') की आवश्यकता होती है। 'A' का उपयोग singular और non-specific nouns के साथ होता है, जबकि "Himalayas" plural और specific है, इसलिए यह भी गलत है। 
 'The'will be used because "Himalayas" is a proper noun that refers to a specific and unique mountain range. 'The' is necessary before nouns that indicate specificity. 'An' is incorrect because it is used with singular nouns starting with a vowel sound, and "Himalayas" is plural. 
 'No article' is incorrect because proper nouns like "Himalayas" typically require a definite article ('The') when referring to a specific entity. 'A' is incorrect because it is used with singular, non-specific nouns, whereas "Himalayas" is plural and specific.

Comprehension: 
 The annual meetings of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), including partner countries like India, as well as the East Asia Summit, took place last week in Laos. These discussions occurred amid escalating conflicts in Europe and the Middle East and rising military tensions in Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, attending his 11th consecutive session at the ASEAN-driven summits, reaffirmed India’s call for military restraint and political reason, reminding world leaders that solutions to global challenges cannot be found on the battlefield. Modi’s visit also marked two significant milestones: The 30th anniversary of India’s “Look East” policy (1994) and the 10th anniversary of his refined “Act East” policy (2014). The context in Asia today, however, is vastly different. In the late 1990s, a sense of great power cooperation and the rise of economic globalisation created favourable conditions for regional institution-building and economic integration under ASEAN’s leadership. This environment also allowed for India’s reintegration with the region. 
 Today, however, great powers are increasingly at odds, and their rivalry is slowing — if not reversing — the trends toward globalisation. China’s regional assertiveness, especially regarding maritime disputes in the South China Sea, has left ASEAN struggling to manage Beijing’s growing military dominance. The region’s fear of China has made it hesitant to fully capitalise on the US’s determination to counter Beijing. Meanwhile, economic de-globalisation is posing new challenges for ASEAN, which has long benefited from US-China commercial cooperation. Compounding these external pressures, ASEAN faces significant internal challenges. The ongoing breakdown of internal order in Myanmar and its military junta’s refusal to engage in constructive dialogue have put the organisation in a difficult position. 
 Where does this leave India in relation to ASEAN? Delhi’s relative standing in the region has risen thanks to its sustained economic growth and growing military capabilities. India’s active membership of the Quad, with Australia, Japan and the US, has given a new edge to India’s regional role. Delhi kept a low profile on regional security issues in the past but is now taking a more affirmative position. PM Modi was unambiguous in opposing China’s expansionism and underlining the importance of Beijing abiding by the rules of the Law of the Sea in managing and resolving maritime disputes in the South China Sea. Over the last decade, India has also expanded bilateral military cooperation with several countries, most notably the Philippines. India’s trade policy with ASEAN, however, remains problematic — although trade has doubled over the last decade to $130 billion, the trade deficit with the region is mounting and now stands at about $44 billion. ASEAN’s economic size ($4 trillion) stands slightly larger than India’s ($3.7 trillion) and its prospects for growth and technological innovation are impressive. Outlining a strategy that focuses on removing internal obstacles and shedding old mindsets against regional trade is critical for an effective long-term Indian role in East Asia. 
 What is the tone of the passage?
cpomains32.explanation:
C)Analytical 
 The passage is focused on examining the current geopolitical situation involving ASEAN, India, and global powers. It analyses the shifts in power dynamics, regional challenges, and India's position. The tone is neutral, fact-based, and provides a reasoned analysis of the subject matter, which makes "Analytical" the most appropriate tone. 
 A: Incorrect, because the passage does not display excessive hope or positivity. While India's growing influence is mentioned, the tone remains factual rather than celebratory. 
 B: Incorrect, as the passage does not harshly criticize any country or policy. It discusses challenges, but without an overtly negative or judgmental tone. 
 D: Incorrect, as there is no use of humor in the passage. The tone is serious and analytical, focusing on global geopolitical issues.

Comprehension: 
 Today, many of us often stress the importance of leisure but that isn’t to downplay the value of earned success and being fully present in the professional world. The workplace is changing due to employees' demands for more freedom and responsibility and a better work-life balance. As a result, many of us have witnessed a surge in concepts like “Bare Minimum Mondays,” “Quiet Quitting,” “Lazy Girl Jobs”, and “The Great Resignation.” Nonetheless, these developments have sparked extensive discussion about the ethical implications for the workplace. 
 Several factors such as lack of trust, lack of consistency, lack of feeling valued, lack of feeling neglected and not being communicated create a sense of disconnection and frustration among employees resulting in a sense of numbness and discontentment in career and eventually seep into personal lives, just as burnout. 
 The term Quiet Quitting or intense dissatisfaction has taken the world by storm, due to the impact of the pandemic, with many workers beginning to reconsider their priorities and boundaries in the workplace. In the early 2020s, driven largely by social media, the term ‘quiet quitting’ emerged as a much-publicized trend in the United States and elsewhere. 
 The term refers to a situation where employees disengage from their jobs or the organization without openly expressing their dissatisfaction or resignation. Instead, they become emotionally detached and disinterested, which leads to reduced productivity, decreased morale and ultimately a decision to leave the company quietly. It is not always a coordinated or planned move conducted by a group of workers to express their displeasure with the organization’s policy rather a subtle form of withdrawal, often overlooked but with significant implications for organizations and individuals alike. There are multifaceted root causes of quitting. Some feel a lack of recognition and reward is the cause, while some blame poor management. 
 Nowadays, the occurrence has amassed a sizable following on social media and is now seen as a movement. Studies and research have shown that around 59% of workers worldwide are ‘quite quitting’ estimated to be costing the global economy $8.8 trillion. Employers must build relationships with their employees so that they can be treated fairly. Being valued at work can prevent employees from experiencing burnout and various health issues arising from being unhappy at their jobs. Employees need to see a clear path to advancement, they may lose motivation and engagement. 
 Remember every worker, every employee working in the organization has a different circumstance within their workplace. Quiet quitting can lead a few to decreased productivity and creativity and at the same time can also impact mental health, causing stress and dissatisfaction. Addressing these factors requires fostering a workplace culture built on trust, consistency, appreciation, a sense of belonging and effective communication. Only when these psychological needs are met, employees will be more likely to engage with their work, thereby reducing the risk of quitting and turnover. When an employee feels motivated, happy, challenged and optimistic, will they be much more likely to expend additional efforts, work a little harder, stay a little longer and above all carry a positive attitude. People do matter. Don’t let them quit.
 What is the tone of the passage regarding the phenomenon of "Quiet Quitting" in the workplace?
cpomains32.explanation:
C) Analytical 
 The passage adopts an analytical tone as it examines the phenomenon of "Quiet Quitting" in the workplace. It provides an in-depth analysis of the causes, effects, and potential solutions to this issue, highlighting the need for a workplace culture built on trust, consistency, and appreciation. The author does not express a positive or negative judgment but rather presents a detailed examination of the topic.

The workplace is changing due to employees' demands for more freedom and responsibility and a better work-life balance. As a result, many of us have witnessed a surge in concepts like “Bare Minimum Mondays,” “Quiet Quitting,” “Lazy Girl Jobs”, and “The Great Resignation.” Nonetheless, these developments have sparked extensive discussion about the ethical implications for the workplace. 
 Several factors such as lack of trust, lack of consistency, lack of feeling valued, lack of feeling neglected and not being communicated create a sense of disconnection and frustration among employees resulting in a sense of numbness and discontentment in career and eventually seep into personal lives, just as burnout. 
 The term Quiet Quitting or intense dissatisfaction has taken the world by storm, due to the impact of the pandemic, with many workers beginning to reconsider their priorities and boundaries in the workplace. In the early 2020s, driven largely by social media, the term ‘quiet quitting’ emerged as a much-publicized trend in the United States and elsewhere. 
 The term refers to a situation where employees disengage from their jobs or the organization without openly expressing their dissatisfaction or resignation. Instead, they become emotionally detached and disinterested, which leads to reduced productivity, decreased morale and ultimately a decision to leave the company quietly. It is not always a coordinated or planned move conducted by a group of workers to express their displeasure with the organization’s policy rather a subtle form of withdrawal, often overlooked but with significant implications for organizations and individuals alike. There are multifaceted root causes of quitting. Some feel a lack of recognition and reward is the cause, while some blame poor management. 
 Nowadays, the occurrence has amassed a sizable following on social media and is now seen as a movement. Studies and research have shown that around 59% of workers worldwide are ‘quite quitting’ estimated to be costing the global economy $8.8 trillion. Employers must build relationships with their employees so that they can be treated fairly. Being valued at work can prevent employees from experiencing burnout and various health issues arising from being unhappy at their jobs. Employees need to see a clear path to advancement, they may lose motivation and engagement. 
 Remember every worker, every employee working in the organization has a different circumstance within their workplace. Quiet quitting can lead a few to decreased productivity and creativity and at the same time can also impact mental health, causing stress and dissatisfaction. Addressing these factors requires fostering a workplace culture built on trust, consistency, appreciation, a sense of belonging and effective communication. Only when these psychological needs are met, employees will be more likely to engage with their work, thereby reducing the risk of quitting and turnover. When an employee feels motivated, happy, challenged and optimistic, will they be much more likely to expend additional efforts, work a little harder, stay a little longer and above all carry a positive attitude. People do matter. Don’t let them quit. 
 What is the main theme of the passage?
options: The importance of leisure in the workplace
The ethical implications of quiet quitting
The impact of social media on employee behavior
The need for a supportive workplace culture
cpomains32.explanation:
D) The need for a supportive workplace culture 
 The main theme of the passage is the need for a supportive workplace culture that addresses employees' psychological needs. The passage emphasizes building trust, consistency, appreciation, and effective communication to prevent quiet quitting and promote employee engagement and satisfaction.

cpomains32.word:
Comprehension: 
 Today, mental health has emerged as one of the biggest concerns in the world. Youth had something to look forward to in the previous generations. They explored the world and gradually discovered new things. Today, due to the internet, those experiences are available at our fingertips with little effort.
With all experiences and stimuli arriving so quickly, they feel lost and unsure of where to go. So, there is a natural seeking for happiness. The pursuit of happiness starts at a much younger age today. However, if they are not given the right direction or philosophy in life, aggression and depression can set in. 
 We are not taught how to handle negative emotions at school or at home. We teach dental hygiene but forget to teach mental hygiene. Stress does not go away by just talking or advising. We need to learn some techniques and tools to get rid of stress and calm the mind. This is where meditation and breathing techniques can play an important role. They are the tools that help you calm your mind and make you feel happy from within. The goal of spirituality is to bring such happiness, which nobody can take away from you. 
 There are two types of happiness: The first is of grabbing or taking. A child enjoys taking things. This is an infant happiness, the desire to possess. The joy of giving is much more fulfilling than the joy of receiving. Have you noticed how happy we feel when we share? For instance, when you see a good movie, you want to tell everybody about it, even recommend that they see it. The movie maker is not giving you any commission to do that; you just feel your loved ones should have the same experience. This is a mature joy that comes from giving. 
 Graduating from the mindset of taking to giving purifies the mind and brings immense joy. On days when you feel hopeless and low, get out of your room and ask people, ‘What can I do for you?’ The service you offer will bring a revolution within. 
 When you engage yourself in helping others, you realise that the Divine is taking care of you very well, and life gets filled with love and gratitude. 
 The willingness to share what we have and to help others without expecting anything in return is called seva. It connects us to others and dissolves barriers that separate our happiness from their happiness. Meditation and seva purify your mind and actions. They are, however, not one-time actions but are to be done repeatedly. Make it a habit. With a few minutes of daily meditation and pranayam, we can cleanse our minds of negative emotions and effectively address mental illness and depression. 
 Despite our meditation practices, when we feel discomfort, we should do something to bring happiness and comfort to others. We can serve others in endless ways. Serving in whatever possible way – contributing our time, donating money, or just speaking about positive things – will change our consciousness. When service becomes your life’s purpose, it eliminates fear, you experience long-term joy, and your mind finds peace. 
 What is the tone of the passage?
cpomains32.explanation:
A) Philosophical and Reflective 
 A: The passage discusses deep concepts about happiness, mental health, and the practice of giving versus taking. It reflects on life lessons and spiritual teachings in a calm and thoughtful manner, making it philosophical and reflective. 
 B: The passage does not contain any sarcastic remarks or dismissive tones. Instead, it offers solutions and positive insights, which are contrary to sarcasm. 
 C: While the passage does critique certain aspects like the lack of mental hygiene education, it is not done in a hostile or overly critical manner. The tone is constructive rather than harsh. 
 D: There is no humor or light-heartedness in the passage. It addresses serious issues like mental health and spirituality, making it a serious and reflective piece.

Comprehension: 
 The Upanishads and Bhagwad Gita talk of universal love. Is it possible? How can I love a child on the street as much as my own child? Love my parents or spouse same way as some stranger? If we define love as feeling, then it is not possible. We have different feelings towards different people. 
 However, universal love is possible as an outcome of understanding our connection with everything else. If we analyse the emotion of love, it is an expression of our deep connection. We end up loving the person in whose presence we feel accepted, connected, cared for, and completely validated. On the other hand, loss of connection with others leads to our feeling deep void, emptiness, loneliness, sadness or grief. According to the Gita and Upanishads, connection is the reality of the universe. The whole world is one vast, intelligent cosmic order, which connects us to everyone and everything. 
 For example, the iron in haemoglobin molecule, which runs in our blood comes from iron particles that were released by the collision of stars. The food that we eat is quietly produced by plant kingdom with the help of sun, water, and earth. The houses that we live in, the cars in which we travel, the entire economic, social and physical infra available to us are an outcome of contribution of countless people whose names and identities are not known to us. The world is a vast network of connection, and our existence is deeply intertwined with everyone else through the intelligent order – Ishvara. 
 If we are alive to this connection, our lives are lived with different expressions of love. We understand that all our accomplishments can be attributed to countless factors, including our efforts, contribution of parents, teachers, friends, and employees. cpomains32.word:
Comprehension:
Are you clear – as clear as in the knowledge a cobra is poisonous – that thought can never under any circumstances reach intelligence? People are using thought to create a machine that can think, a supercomputer, and artificial intelligence. They are working to create a brain that will be like ours, which will be mechanical. They are using their tremendous knowledge of the brain to produce an artificial brain which is based on thought.
Do you see this as a fact? To see it as a fact is to see that thought under no circumstances can have the other. If thought is no longer the instrument of inquiry, then you have nothing else with which to inquire. You can’t inquire. Then what is intelligence that is not based on inquiry?
I want to inquire into truth. I don’t know anything about it. I don’t want to depend on anyone to find out. So, I have to discard all of the past. I want to find out what supreme intelligence is. So, can I discard everything that I know? The only instrument I have is thought. I can think clearly because I have been trained to think not sentimentally but objectively. Thinking which can produce so-called intelligence is then on the same level as thinking that has produced war. Therefore, it is not intelligence. So, under no circumstances will thinking have a perception of that. I must be absolutely clear. If I am not clear unconsciously, deeply, then thought is going to interfere.
Before anything else, I want to clear the board. Is that possible? I see that what they are doing won’t get them there. They will create mechanical, artificial intelligence, which is like human intelligence. That is capable of destroying the world. Thinking, and all the instruments thought has invented to investigate into that – meditation, various types of silence, various types of self-denial – are out. The technologies won’t accept that, but true inquiry is that. And they haven’t found it. They are anchored to thought, and they move through thought. They won’t accept that thought can under no circumstances come to it. Then what have I left to see that thought, under any circumstances, cannot produce intelligence?
 What is the tone of the passage?
cpomains32.explanation:
A) Critical and Analytical 
 A: The passage critically examines the limitations of thought and its inability to reach true intelligence. It provides an analytical perspective by questioning the role of thought in understanding intelligence. 
 B: The passage does not encourage any positive outcomes or solutions but instead focuses on highlighting the limitations of thought. 
 C: The tone is not indifferent, as the author is actively engaged in explaining the nuances of the topic and seems deeply involved in presenting their viewpoint. 
 D: While the passage acknowledges the limitations of thought, it is not hopeless but rather focused on understanding the nature of intelligence.

Comprehension: 
 Following the disappointment of several near-misses in the recent Olympics, India’s best-ever show of 29 medals for an 18th place finish in the Paris Paralympics is reason to celebrate. From four medals and 43rd spot in Rio 2016 to 19 medals and 24th rank in Tokyo 2020, this is a significant ascent and depicts the Indian Paralympians’ constant improvement in sync with the increased government support. Since the challenges are different, it may not be fair to compare the achievements of the para-athletes with those in the Olympics. India’s performance in the 2024 Paralympics reflects its para-athletes’ quest for excellence despite the unimaginable odds they face. Of the seven gold, nine silver and 13 bronze medals, the majority (17 in all), came from para-athletics. The javelin throwers and high jumpers contributed the most, with four medals in different categories classified as impairments. Para-badminton (five), para-shooting (four), para-archery (two) and para-judo (one) completed the country’s medal tally. Shooter Avani Lekhara and javelin thrower Sumit Antil, who set a new Paralympic record, defended their gold medals, high jumper Mariyappan Thangavelu claimed his third successive medal, 17-year-old armless archer Sheetal Devi became the youngest Indian to win a medal and Harvinder Singh won the first para-archery gold. 
 Preethi Pal bagged India’s first-ever track medal as she picked up a bronze in women’s 100m T35 event followed by another in 200m and Kapil Parmar captured India’s first para-judo medal. Nagaland’s 40-year-old Army man Hokato Sema, who shone as a shot putter despite losing a leg in the line of duty in the prime of his youth, cornered glory to underscore the indomitable human spirit. Overall, the spectators’ response to the Paralympics 2024 was heart-warming — organisers sold over two million tickets for the Games.  'Lead'will be used because it refers to the material inside a pencil tip used for writing. The sentence talks about what the pencil tip is made of, so 'Lead' is the correct choice. cpomains33.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive form. 
 The shopkeeper lifted the shutter to open his shop.
options: To open his shop, the shutter is lifted by the shopkeeper.
The shutter was lifted by the shopkeeper to open his shop.
The shutter is being lifted by the shopkeeper to open his shop.
The shutter will be lifted by the shopkeeper to open his shop.
cpomains33.explanation:
B)The shutter was lifted by the shopkeeper to open his shop 
 Active वाक्य का Object Passive वाक्य का Subject बन जाता है। Verb को Active से Passive में बदलते समय सही Tense का प्रयोग किया जाता है। Active वाक्य में "The shopkeeper" Subject है, "lifted" Verb (Past Simple) है और "the shutter" Object है। Passive में बदलने पर Object "The shutter" Subject बन गया है। Verb को "was lifted" (Past Simple Passive) में बदला गया है और "by the shopkeeper" के रूप में Agent के रूप में प्रयोग किया गया है। Passive वाक्य: The shutter was lifted by the shopkeeper to open his shop. 
 To change a sentence from Active to Passive Voice: The object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence. The verb is transformed from the active form to the passive form, ensuring correct tense usage. In this case, "The shopkeeper" (Subject), "lifted" (Verb in Past Simple), and "the shutter" (Object) from the active voice have been transformed into "The shutter" (Subject), "was lifted" (Passive Verb in Past Simple), and "by the shopkeeper" (Agent). Passive Sentence: The shutter was lifted by the shopkeeper to open his shop.

Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. 
 He exclaimed with delight that he had won the first prize.
options: “Hurrah! I will win the first prize,” said he.
“Hurrah! I have won the first prize,” said he.
“Hurrah! I win the first prize,” said he.
“Wow! I might win the first prize,” said he.
cpomains33.explanation:
B) “Hurrah! I have won the first prize,” said he. 
 Direct से Indirect Speech में बदलने पर Reporting Verb और Reported Speech का सही use किया जाता है। यहाँ वाक्य में "He exclaimed with delight" Reporting Verb है और "that he had won the first prize" Reported Speech है। इसे Direct Speech में बदलते समय निम्नलिखित नियमों का पालन किया गया है: "Hurrah!" खुशी के भाव को व्यक्त करता है, इसलिए इसे Direct Speech में "Hurrah!" के रूप में लिखा गया। "he had won" (Past Perfect) को Direct Speech में "I have won" (Present Perfect) में परिवर्तित किया गया, क्योंकि Direct में वक्ता खुद के बारे में बात कर रहा है। सही विकल्प वही होगा जो खुशी के भाव और Present Perfect Tense को सही ढंग से व्यक्त करे। 
 When converting from Indirect to Direct Speech, the Reporting Verb and Reported Speech must be reconstructed accurately. In this case, "He exclaimed with delight" is the Reporting Verb, and "that he had won the first prize" is the Reported Speech. The transformation to Direct Speech follows these rules: "Hurrah!" is used to express joy, so it is written as "Hurrah!" in Direct Speech. "he had won" (Past Perfect) changes to "I have won" (Present Perfect) in Direct Speech because the speaker refers to himself. The correct option must convey joy and use the Present Perfect tense properly.

A) These introductions came through an amendment made to the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, or IT Rules
B)  Should social media intermediaries fail to prevent users from hosting or publishing information that have been flagged as false by the fact check unit, they stand to lose their “safe harbour” immunity
C)  Online content that concerns the central government’s business in any manner

She tells her friend, “I have been studying for my examination.”
She told her friend, “I was studying for my examination.”
cpomains33.explanation:
D)She told her friend, “I was studying for my examination.” 
 Indirect से Direct Speech में बदलते समय Tense और Pronouns का सही रूप में प्रयोग किया जाता है। दिए गए Indirect वाक्य में "She told her friend" Reporting Verb है, जो Past Tense में है। इसलिए Reported Speech का Tense भी Past Form में रहेगा। Reported Speech में "she had been studying" (Past Perfect Continuous) को Direct Speech में बदलते समय "was studying" (Past Continuous) में बदला जाएगा, क्योंकि Past Perfect Continuous Tense को Direct Speech में Past Continuous Tense में बदला जाता है। सही वाक्य है: "She told her friend, ‘I was studying for my examination.’" 
 When converting from Indirect to Direct Speech, the tense and pronouns must be appropriately transformed. In the given Indirect sentence, "She told her friend" is the reporting verb in the past tense, so the tense of the reported speech must also remain in a past form. The phrase "she had been studying" (Past Perfect Continuous) in the Indirect Speech is converted to "was studying" (Past Continuous) in the Direct Speech. This is because Past Perfect Continuous Tense in Indirect Speech becomes Past Continuous Tense in Direct Speech. 
 The correct sentence is: "She told her friend, ‘I was studying for my examination.’"

 Active से Passive Voice में बदलने के लिए, Passive वाक्य का Subject Active वाक्य का Object बन जाता है। Verb को Passive से Active में बदलते समय सही Tense और Modal Verb का प्रयोग किया जाता है। Passive वाक्य में "Parents" Subject है, "should be respected" Verb (Modal Verb with Passive Structure) है, और "by their children" Agent है। Active में बदलने पर Agent "Children" Subject बन गया है और Verb "should respect" (Modal Verb with Active Structure) में बदल गई है। इसलिए Active वाक्य होगा: "Children should respect their parents." 
 To change a sentence from Passive to Active Voice, the subject of the passive sentence becomes the object of the active sentence. The verb is transformed from the passive structure to the active form, ensuring correct modal usage. In this case, "Parents" (Subject), "should be respected" (Verb in Modal Passive), and "by their children" (Agent) from the passive sentence have been transformed into "Children" (Subject), "should respect" (Active Verb with Modal), and "their parents" (Object). Thus, the active sentence is: "Children should respect their parents."

 'Laid'will be used because it is the past tense of 'lay,' which means "to put something down carefully." The sentence describes placing 'keys' on the 'kitchen counter,' indicating a past action.  When converting a sentence to Indirect Speech, the tense of the Reported Speech is adjusted based on the tense of the Reporting Verb. Here, the Reporting Verb "said" is in Past Tense, so the verb in the Reported Speech should be in Past Perfect Tense. In the Direct Sentence, "I lost my umbrella" (Past Tense) becomes "she had lost her umbrella" in Indirect Speech, with "I" replaced by "she" according to the subject "Gita," and "lost" changed to "had lost" (Past Perfect).

 Active से Passive Voice में बदलने के लिए, प्रश्नवाचक वाक्य में भी वही प्रक्रिया लागू होती है। Active वाक्य में "Who" Subject है, "built" Verb (Past Simple) है और "this colossal architectural structure" Object है। Passive में बदलते समय, Object "this colossal architectural structure" को Subject बनाया गया है, Verb को "was built" (Past Simple Passive) में बदला गया है, और "By whom" प्रश्नवाचक वाक्य की संरचना बनाए रखने के लिए प्रयोग किया गया है। 
 To change the sentence from Active to Passive Voice in an interrogative sentence, the same process is applied. In the active voice, "Who" is the subject, "built" is the verb in the Past Simple tense, and "this colossal architectural structure" is the object. In the passive transformation, the object "this colossal architectural structure" becomes the subject, the verb is converted to "was built" (Past Simple Passive), and "By whom" is used to maintain the interrogative structure.

cpomains33.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech. 
 My friend said to me, “Do you want to accompany us on this tour?”
options: My friend asked me if I wanted to accompany them on that tour.
My friend asked me if I wanted to accompany us on that tour.
My friend asked me if he wanted to accompany them on that tour.
My friend asked me if I wanted to accompany them on that tour?
cpomains33.explanation:
A)My friend asked me if I wanted to accompany them on that tour 
 Reported Speech में बदलते समय, Direct Speech का वाक्य Indirect Speech में बदलता है। इसमें Reporting Verb ("said to") को Reporting Verb ("asked") में बदल दिया गया है क्योंकि यह एक प्रश्न है। Direct Speech में वाक्य एक प्रश्न था, और Indirect Speech में इसे एक कथन के रूप में बदल दिया गया है। "Do you want" (Present Simple) को Indirect Speech में "wanted" (Past Simple) में बदल दिया गया है क्योंकि Reporting Verb Past में है। "us" (Direct Speech में) को "them" (Indirect Speech में) में बदल दिया गया है क्योंकि यह दूसरे समूह को इंगित करता है। "this tour" (Direct Speech में) को "that tour" (Indirect Speech में) में बदल दिया गया है क्योंकि यह समय और स्थान बदलने का संकेत देता है। विकल्प A सही है क्योंकि यह सभी आवश्यक परिवर्तन सही ढंग से दिखाता है। 
 When converting Direct Speech to Indirect Speech, the sentence is transformed from a direct question to a reported statement. The Reporting Verb "said to" is changed to "asked" because it is a question. The verb "Do you want" (Present Simple) in Direct Speech changes to "wanted" (Past Simple) in Indirect Speech as the Reporting Verb is in the past tense. "us" in Direct Speech changes to "them" in Indirect Speech to refer to the other group. "this tour" in Direct Speech changes to "that tour" in Indirect Speech, indicating a shift in time and place. Option A is correct as it accurately reflects all these changes.

cpomains33.word:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. 
 The Indian Government has launched the National Rural Livelihoods Mission, a _________ programme aimed at reducing rural poverty.
cpomains33.explanation:
A)'Flagship'का use होगा क्योंकि 'flagship' का अर्थ है "किसी संगठन या सरकार का सबसे प्रमुख या महत्वपूर्ण कार्यक्रम"। sentence में यह स्पष्ट है कि राष्ट्रीय ग्रामीण आजीविका मिशन एक महत्वपूर्ण और मुख्य कार्यक्रम है जो ग्रामीण गरीबी को कम करने के उद्देश्य से शुरू किया गया है। 'Designer' का अर्थ है "डिजाइन किया गया" या "फैशन से संबंधित", जो इस संदर्भ में सही नहीं है। 'Regressive' का अर्थ है "प्रतिक्रियावादी" या "विकास को पीछे ले जाने वाला", जो इस सकारात्मक पहल के लिए उपयुक्त नहीं है। 'Controversial' का अर्थ है "विवादास्पद", जो इस संदर्भ में गलत है क्योंकि वाक्य कार्यक्रम को विवादास्पद नहीं दिखाता। 
 Flagship'will be the correct as it means "the most important or prominent program of an organization or government." The sentence clearly conveys that the National Rural Livelihoods Mission is a significant and main program aimed at reducing rural poverty. 'Designer' means "created by a designer" or "related to fashion," which doesn't fit this context. 'Regressive' means "moving backward or counterproductive," which is inappropriate for this positive initiative. 
 'Controversial' means "causing public disagreement or debate," which is incorrect as the sentence does not indicate any controversy.

cpomains33.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. 
 The student requested them to take him to the reception
options: Please take me in the reception,” said the student.
“Take me to the reception,” said the student.
“Take me to the reception now,” said the student.
“Please take me to the reception," said the student
cpomains33.explanation:
D) “Please take me to the reception," said the student 
 यह वाक्य Direct Speech में बदलने के लिए Indirect Speech से वाक्य की संरचना को समझना आवश्यक है। दिए गए Indirect वाक्य "The student requested them to take him to the reception" में Subject "The student" है, Reporting Verb "requested" है और Reported Speech "to take him to the reception" है। Direct Speech में इसे बदलते समय Reporting Verb "requested" को वाक्य के अनुरूप "Please" के साथ बदल दिया जाता है। Reported Speech को उद्धरण चिह्न (“”) के अंदर रखा जाता है। सही वाक्य होगा: "Please take me to the reception," said the student. 
 To transform this sentence into Direct Speech, we need to analyze the structure of the Indirect Sentence. In the given sentence, "The student requested them to take him to the reception," the subject is "The student," the reporting verb is "requested," and the reported speech is "to take him to the reception." While converting into Direct Speech, the reporting verb "requested" is appropriately replaced with "Please," and the reported speech is placed within quotation marks (“”). The correct sentence becomes: "Please take me to the reception," said the student.

B) ‘Forth'का use होगा क्योंकि "forth" का अर्थ होता है "आगे" या "प्रकट होना।" Sentence में कहा गया है कि जब भी उसे संबोधित किया जाता है, वह आगे आती है और अपनी जिम्मेदारी (role) को अच्छे तरीके से निभाती है। इसलिए 'forth' यहाँ सही है।‘Role'का अर्थ होता है "किसी की जिम्मेदारी या कार्य।" यह वाक्य के अर्थ के साथ पूरी तरह से मेल खाता है क्योंकि वाक्य में उसके कर्तव्यों की चर्चा हो रही हैFourth'का अर्थ है"चौथा," जो इस वाक्य के संदर्भ में बिल्कुल उपयुक्त नहीं है क्योंकि वाक्य में किसी क्रम की बात नहीं हो रही है।Roll'का अर्थ है"घुमाना"या"रोटीकाटुकड़ा," जो"अपनीजिम्मेदारीनिभाने"केसंदर्भमेंफिटनहींहोता।Fourth'गलत है क्योंकि यह संख्या को दर्शाता है, और'Roll'गलत है क्योंकि यह कार्य या भूमिका के संदर्भ में सही नहीं है। 
 'Forth' will be used because it means "forward" or "to emerge." The sentence indicates that whenever she is addressed, she steps forward and performs her duties. 
 'Role' is correct because it means a person's responsibility or duty, aligning perfectly with the context.'Fourth'means "the fourth in a sequence," which does not make sense in the context of stepping forward or emerging.'Roll'means "to move by turning over" or refers to a "physical object like bread roll," which does not fit the context of performing duties.'Fourth'is incorrect as it denotes a sequence, and'Roll'is irrelevant in the context of responsibilities or duties.

cpomains33.word:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. 
 The manager swiftly overtook him, ____________ effortlessly past the skinny Englishman, with a practiced ease.
cpomains33.explanation:
A)Slidingका use होगा क्योंकि "sliding" का अर्थ होता है चुपचाप या आसानी से सरकना, जो इस sentence में contextually सही है। sentence में mention है कि प्रबंधक ने अपनी कुशलता से "skinny Englishman" को आसानी से पार किया, इसलिए 'sliding' यहाँ सही है। Dawdling (धीरे-धीरे चलना या समय बर्बाद करना) इस context में गलत है क्योंकि प्रबंधक का कार्य कुशलता और तेजी से किया गया है, न कि धीमी गति से। Kindling (जलाना या प्रज्वलित करना) का इस वाक्य के संदर्भ में कोई अर्थ नहीं बनता है। Rendering (प्रस्तुत करना या बनाना) का भी इस संदर्भ में उपयोग अनुचित है क्योंकि यहाँ प्रबंधक का कार्य गति और सहजता से सरकने का है। 
 Slidingis grammatically correct because it implies moving smoothly and easily, which matches the context where the manager moves past with practiced ease. The verb aligns with the sentence's depiction of fluid and skilled motion. Dawdling means wasting time or moving slowly, which contradicts the quick and efficient motion described in the sentence. Kindling refers to starting a fire or igniting something, which is irrelevant here. Rendering means to provide or depict something, which doesn't align with the context of physical motion.

cpomains33.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive form. 
 Who took Bruno for a walk?
options: By whom has Bruno been taken for a walk?

By whom will Bruno be taken for a walk?

B)By whom was Bruno taken for a walk? 
 Active वाक्य में "Who" Subject है, "took" Verb (Past Simple Tense) है, और "Bruno" Object है। Passive में बदलने के लिए Object "Bruno" को Subject बनाया जाएगा। Verb "took" को Passive Voice के Past Simple Tense में बदलकर "was taken" लिखा जाएगा। "By whom" का प्रयोग Active वाक्य के Subject "Who" को Passive में बदलने के लिए किया जाएगा। 
 In the active sentence, "Who" is the subject, "took" is the verb (Past Simple Tense), and "Bruno" is the object. To transform it into the passive voice, the object "Bruno" becomes the subject. The verb "took" is changed into the passive form "was taken" to reflect the Past Simple Tense. "By whom" is used to convert the subject "Who" into the passive form.

 S: The use of the word "Surprisingly" indicates a continuation of the thought in sentence P. The pronoun "It" in the phrase "It did not stop there." refers back to the narrator's experience with running, which is discussed in sentences R and P. So, S should follow P.

cpomains33.word:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. 
 My sister requested me to bring her a watch
options: She said, “My sister, please bring me a watch.”
“Please bring my sister a watch,” said she.
“Please bring me a watch,” said my sister.
My sister said, “Will you bring me a watch?”
cpomains33.explanation:
C)“Please bring me a watch,” said my sister 
 Direct Speech में वाक्य को बदलने के लिए, Indirect Speech में दिए गए वाक्य का मूल संदर्भ और भाव Direct Speech में शामिल किया जाता है। दिए गए वाक्य "My sister requested me to bring her a watch" में "requested" को देखकर यह स्पष्ट है कि Direct Speech में वाक्य अनुरोध (request) के रूप में होगा। वाक्य का Subject "My sister" है, और Object "me" है, जिसे Direct Speech में "said my sister" के रूप में बदला गया है। "Bring her a watch" को Direct Speech में बदलते समय "her" को "me" के रूप में लिया जाता है, क्योंकि यह मेरी बहन स्वयं के लिए घड़ी मांग रही है। 
 To convert the sentence into Direct Speech, the original context and intent from the Indirect Speech sentence must be retained. In the sentence "My sister requested me to bring her a watch," the word "requested" indicates that the Direct Speech sentence must represent a request. The subject is "My sister," and the object is "me," which transforms into "said my sister" in Direct Speech. "Bring her a watch" changes to "me" in Direct Speech as the sister is asking for a watch for herself.

cpomains33.word:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in indirect speech. 
 “I have not completed the assignment yet,” the student admitted
options: The student admitted that he/she hadn’t been able to complete the assignment yet.

The student admitted that he/she hadn’t completed the assignment yet.
The student admitted that he/she hasn't been able to complete the assignment yet.
cpomains33.explanation:
C)The student admitted that he/she hadn’t completed the assignment yet. 
 Indirect Speech में बदलने के लिए Direct Speech के वाक्य को Reporting Verb और Reported Speech के आधार पर बदला जाता है। Reporting Verb "admitted" (Past Tense) में है, इसलिए Reported Speech का Tense भी Past में बदल जाएगा। Direct Speech में "I have not completed the assignment yet" (Present Perfect Tense) का उपयोग किया गया है। Indirect Speech में इसे Past Perfect Tense में बदलकर "he/she hadn’t completed the assignment yet" लिखा जाएगा। 
 To change a sentence from Direct to Indirect Speech, the Reported Speech is transformed based on the Reporting Verb and its tense. Here, the Reporting Verb "admitted" is in the Past Tense, so the tense of the Reported Speech must shift to a corresponding past form. 
 In the Direct Speech, "I have not completed the assignment yet" is in Present Perfect Tense. In Indirect Speech, it changes to Past Perfect Tense as "he/she hadn’t completed the assignment yet."

 Direct Speech में वाक्य को बदलने के लिए ध्यान देना होता है कि Reported Speech का समय और शब्द सही ढंग से बदले जाएँ। यहाँ वाक्य में "Tom said that he had a strange experience the day before" Indirect Speech में है। इसमें: "he had" (Past Perfect) को Direct Speech में "I had" (Past Simple) में बदला गया है। "the day before" (Indirect में प्रयुक्त समय) को "yesterday" (Direct में प्रयुक्त समय) में बदला गया है। 
 To convert the given sentence into Direct Speech, we need to ensure that the Reported Speech is correctly transformed: "he had" (Past Perfect in Indirect Speech) is converted to "I had" (Past Simple in Direct Speech).  When converting from Direct to Indirect Speech, personal pronouns and time indicators must be appropriately changed. In this sentence, "The principal said" is the reporting verb, and "he would hold a meeting the next day" is the reported speech. Here, "he" changes to "I," and "the next day" changes to "tomorrow." Option C correctly converts the sentence into Direct Speech. It follows the correct sequence of using the reporting verb after a comma and quotation marks.

cpomains33.word:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. 
 As technology evolves, consumers increasingly _______________ products with enhanced features and greater efficiency.
cpomains33.explanation:
A)Demand'का use सही है क्योंकि यह एक सामान्य सत्य (general truth) और वर्तमान आदत (present habit) को व्यक्त करता है, जिसमें बताया गया है कि जैसे-जैसे तकनीक विकसित होती है, उपभोक्ता बेहतर सुविधाओं और अधिक कार्यक्षमता वाले उत्पादों की मांग करते हैं। 'Has demanded' गलत है क्योंकि यह वर्तमान आदत के बजाय अतीत में पूरी हुई क्रिया (completed action in the past) को व्यक्त करता है। 'Were demanding' गलत है क्योंकि यह अतीत में जारी प्रक्रिया (past continuous action) को व्यक्त करता है, जो यहाँ प्रासंगिक नहीं है।'Might demand' गलत है क्योंकि यह संभाव्यता (possibility) को व्यक्त करता है, जबकि वाक्य एक सामान्य सत्य को व्यक्त करता है। 
 Demand'is correct because it expresses a general truth or present habit, indicating that as technology evolves, consumers seek products with better features and efficiency. 
 'Has demanded' is incorrect because it refers to a completed action in the past, which does not align with the ongoing trend described. 'Were demanding' is incorrect as it denotes a past continuous action, which is irrelevant here. 'Might demand' is incorrect because it implies possibility rather than a general truth.

 Active Voice में बदलने के लिए, Passive वाक्य के Object को Active वाक्य में शामिल करना होता है और Verb को आदेश या निर्देश के रूप में व्यवस्थित किया जाता है। Passive वाक्य "Let the door be closed" में: "The door" (Object) Passive वाक्य का मुख्य भाग है। "be closed" (Verb in Passive form) को Active में बदलने पर "Close the door" (Verb in Imperative form) बन जाता है। Passive वाक्य में आदेश का तात्पर्य Active में सीधे निर्देश देने से है। इसलिए, Active वाक्य "Close the door" (D) सही उत्तर है।

 Active से Passive Voice में बदलने के लिए, Passive वाक्य का Subject Active वाक्य का Object बन जाता है। Verb को Passive से Active में बदलते समय सही Tense का प्रयोग किया जाता है। Passive वाक्य "Was your bicycle stolen by him?" में "Your bicycle" Subject है, "was stolen" Verb (Past Indefinite Passive) है और "by him" Agent है। Active वाक्य में बदलने पर Subject "He" बन जाएगा, Verb "stole" (Past Indefinite Active) में परिवर्तित होगी और Object "your bicycle" रहेगा। सही वाक्य होगा: "Did he steal your bicycle?"। 
 To change a sentence from Passive to Active Voice, the subject of the passive sentence becomes the object in the active sentence. The verb is transformed from the passive form to the active form, ensuring correct tense usage. In the passive sentence "Was your bicycle stolen by him?", "Your bicycle" is the subject, "was stolen" is the verb in Past Indefinite Passive, and "by him" is the agent. 
 In the active sentence, the subject becomes "He," the verb changes to "stole" (Past Indefinite Active), and the object remains "your bicycle." The correct sentence is: "Did he steal your bicycle?"

 “You were warned by us three days ago,” the manager shouted at him.
options: The manager shouted at him that he was warned by them three days before.

 Direct से Indirect Speech में बदलने के लिए: Reporting Verb (shouted) का Tense परिवर्तन नहीं होता है। Reported Speech में Verb का परिवर्तन Past Perfect Tense में किया जाता है, क्योंकि Original Statement Past Simple Tense में है ("You were warned"). "three days ago" को Indirect Speech में "three days before" में बदल दिया जाता है, क्योंकि समय की अभिव्यक्ति Reporting Speech के समय के सापेक्ष होती है। इस प्रकार, "You were warned by us three days ago" को Indirect Speech में "he had been warned by them three days before" में बदला जाएगा। 
 To change Direct Speech into Indirect Speech: The Reporting Verb ("shouted") remains unchanged as it is already in Past Tense. The verb in the Reported Speech ("were warned") is changed to Past Perfect Tense ("had been warned") because the original statement is in Past Simple Tense. The time expression "three days ago" changes to "three days before" in Indirect Speech to reflect relative time. Thus, "You were warned by us three days ago" transforms into "he had been warned by them three days before" in Indirect Speech.

 Direct से Indirect Speech में बदलने के नियम (Rules for Changing Direct to Indirect Speech):

 Rules for Changing Direct to Indirect Speech:

cpomains33.word:
Select the option that correctly expresses the following sentence in indirect speech. 
 Ritu said, “I am eating apples.”
options: Ritu said that she was eating apples.
Ritu told that she was eating apples.
Ritu said that she has been eating apples.
Ritu said that she had been eating apples.
cpomains33.explanation:
A)Ritu said that she was eating apples. 
 Direct वाक्य में "Ritu said," Reporting Verb है, और "I am eating apples" Reported Speech है। Present Continuous Tense ("am eating") को Indirect Speech में बदलते समय, Reporting Verb "said" (Past Tense) के कारण Reported Speech का Tense बदलकर Past Continuous Tense ("was eating") हो जाता है। Personal Pronoun "I" को Reporting Subject "Ritu" के अनुसार "she" में बदला गया है। Conjunction "that" का use Reported Speech को Reporting Verb से जोड़ने के लिए किया गया है। 
 To change a sentence from Direct to Indirect Speech: 
 In the given sentence, "Ritu said," is the Reporting Verb, and "I am eating apples" is the Reported Speech. When transforming into Indirect Speech, the Present Continuous Tense ("am eating") changes to Past Continuous Tense ("was eating") because the Reporting Verb "said" is in the Past Tense. The Personal Pronoun "I" is changed to "she" based on the subject "Ritu." 
 The conjunction "that" is used to connect the Reported Speech with the Reporting Verb.

options: He wished that he was a ruined man.

 Direct Speech में वाक्य है: “Alas!  The Direct Speech sentence “Alas! The Present Tense “I am” is converted to “he was” in the Past Tense, maintaining the sequence of tenses.

Comprehension:
It’s an intriguing paradox — tourism continues to be the prime money-spinner for Himachal Pradesh, yet properties owned by the HP Tourism Development Corporation (HPTDC) are not attracting tourists in droves. The Himachal High Court has ordered the closure of 18 such properties as it is no longer financially viable to run them. The order is aimed at ensuring that public resources are not wasted by the corporation in the upkeep of these ‘white elephants’. With the HPTDC failing to optimally utilise these establishments, the exchequer is bearing the financial burden at a time when the debt-stressed state government is busy tightening the purse strings. 
 The hill state played host to no less than one crore tourists in the first six months of this year, but most of them seem to have preferred private hotels to those operated by the tourism body. This is a sad reflection on the authorities’ commitment to promoting properties at picture-perfect locations in popular as well as remote areas. The HPTDC has allowed matters to drift for too long. It was only recently that its board of directors decided to hand over some of its hotels, restaurants and cafes to private players — with the rider that the state government would continue to have their ownership. This process should be conducted in a fair and transparent manner so that business entities with a proven track record in tourism get a chance to bring about a much-needed turnaround. 
 There is a perception among common tourists that state-run hotels are accessible only to influential people such as politicians and bureaucrats. The HPTDC needs to dispel this notion by reaching out to the masses through a multi-media publicity campaign. The involvement of travel agents and other stakeholders can spur this endeavour. The corporation should also be open to suggestions for putting its house in order and providing quality services to tourists. A ‘business as usual’ approach should make way for proactive and judicious collaboration. 
 Which key action did the Himachal High Court take regarding HPTDC properties?
options: It ordered the privatization of HPTDC properties.
It mandated the closure of 18 properties.
It directed the promotion of state-run hotels.
It declared HPTDC hotels as tourist attractions.
cpomains33.explanation: B)The passage mentions that the Himachal High Court has ordered the closure of 18 properties owned by the HPTDC as these were no longer financially viable. This ensures that public resources are not wasted on maintaining underperforming properties.

Comprehension: 
 It has been a tale of contrasting Indian performances in cricket over the last few weeks. India’s home dominance, especially in Tests, ground to a halt as the visiting New Zealanders swept the series 3-0. However, an entirely different squad under Suryakumar Yadav donned their blue jerseys, flew to South Africa and won the T20I series 3-1. An inexplicable fragility against spin in Tests and a domineering aura in T20Is are evident. While this backstory has its distinct ebb and flow, the next seven weeks should offer an entirely new perspective, besides the attendant hype, as India and Australia clash in the Border-Gavaskar Trophy series with the first Test commencing at Perth’s massive Optus Stadium on Friday (November 22, 2024). With five Tests scheduled across Australia through the southern summer, one of cricket’s greatest rivalries will get a fresh start. While the microscopic tale is centred around how this series would evolve, the macroscopic outlook would be focused on the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) rankings in which India currently trails topper Australia in the points percentage tally. A berth in the WTC final is no longer an automatic choice, and if India wants to qualify on its own merit, it needs to win four of these five Tests, or else await the permutation-combination of results involving other teams. 
 Over the last decade, beyond the subcontinent, India has largely shed its poor-traveller tag and the two Test series triumphs in Australia during the 2018-19 and 2020-21 tours, is a reflection of this resilience. It is this slice of history that adds more bite as Jasprit Bumrah’s men step out for their latest cricketing joust. With regular skipper Rohit Sharma, currently on a paternity break, set to lead from the second Test, India will gain added experience in its ranks. Injury concerns over Shubman Gill, and the absence of Mohammed Shami, wending his way back from a surgery, may add to the worry lines but in the 2020-21 tour, India was literally the walking wounded, and yet Ajinkya Rahane led a second-string unit to a remarkable 2-1 victory. It is this abiding strength in the Indian ranks that has unsettled the Australians, and Pat Cummins and his men are wary of their rivals despite the latest reversal against New Zealand. A lot will hinge on spearhead Bumrah’s spells and the ability of the batters to string vital partnerships. Both Virat Kohli and Rohit are suffering a low patch in Tests and if these seniors can turn it around, India will be better served. An interesting series is on the cards and perhaps new heroes will rise. 
 Which key factor makes the upcoming Border-Gavaskar Trophy significant in the larger context of cricket? 
 i. The rivalry between India and New Zealand 
 ii. The rankings in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) 
 iii. The unpredictability of weather conditions in Australia 
 iv. The possibility of new players being introduced in the Indian team'
cpomains33.explanation: B)The passage emphasizes that the Border-Gavaskar Trophy holds significance not only because of the rivalry between India and Australia but also due to its implications on the ICC World Test Championship rankings, where India trails Australia. The need to win four out of five Tests to secure a berth in the WTC final further underscores its importance. Other options like weather unpredictability and player introduction are not highlighted as central themes.

Comprehension: 
 Tackling global hunger and poverty and promoting climate justice were declared goals for the recent G-20 summit in Rio de Janeiro. Brazilian President Lula Da Silva called poverty a “scourge that shames humanity”, asking the gathered nations to implement policies such as taxing the ‘super-rich’, using a 2% wealth tax on the world’s wealthiest to generate more than $200 billion in revenue. But the G-20 declaration fell short of that. Prime Minister Narendra Modi too underlined that the problems of the world are felt most acutely by the ‘Global South’, and, therefore, that the reins of global administration must belong to those that represent the larger majority in the world. The G-20 hosted by Brazil, was by the third host country of the Global South, after Indonesia in 2022 and India in 2023. The next G-20 is to be in South Africa. The Brazil summit was expected to focus on solutions for the poorer, emerging economies. However, its timing diluted the cause and diffused the focus, given the other issues the world confronts. This was the first G-20 summit since the October 7 attacks on Israel and its reprisals on Gaza and Lebanon. Russia’s invasion of Ukraine had also made forging consensus at Bali and New Delhi already quite difficult. With deepening polarised narratives over both conflicts, the G-20 declaration was watered down, expressing only “deep concern” over the humanitarian situation in Gaza, and dropping all reference to Russia while highlighting the “suffering... with regard to global food and energy security”. It was devoid of specifics on ending the conflicts. 
 The G-20 was also timed closely with the COP29 in Azerbaijan — Brazil will be in 2025 host — indicating that issues of climate financing and climate justice, which have been raised by the developing world, would find place in the G-20 declarations, and then feed into the COP process. However, the summit followed just after the U.S. presidential election results, casting its shadow. Given his moves during his first tenure, Donald Trump will not set much store by the aspirations of the Global South. Nor is he likely to expend the kind of resources expected from the U.S. towards tackling global warming or in curtailing the exploitation of fossil fuels. His cabinet has climate deniers and his own campaign slogan was “Drill, baby, drill”. Given the portents, the Global South, and the quartet of Indonesia-India-Brazil-South Africa, will have to ensure that the next G-20 is able to concretise the concerns of the developing world, and set out a path for the future on poverty and hunger, climate change and global governance. In 2026, as the G-20 will return to the U.S., the deadline is more urgent. 
 Which policy did Brazilian President Lula Da Silva propose at the recent G-20 summit to address global hunger and poverty?
options: Taxing the 'super-rich' with a 2% wealth tax.
cpomains33.explanation: B) In the passage, Brazilian President Lula Da Silva called poverty a “scourge that shames humanity” and proposed implementing policies such as taxing the 'super-rich'. Specifically, he suggested a 2% wealth tax on the world's wealthiest individuals to generate more than $200 billion in revenue to tackle global hunger and poverty.

Comprehension:
Discipline in India is undergoing a transformative shift. In Faridkot, Punjab, a group of rowdy students, who allegedly endangered police officers during a clash recently, were met with an unusual punishment: a week of assisting the traffic police for two hours daily after school. This innovative disciplinary approach aims to teach civic responsibility while deterring future misconduct. In Srinagar, a tragic car accident involving underage drivers in mid-November led to a crackdown on violations. The authorities seized vehicles and implemented stricter licensing policies while counselling parents and students to address the root causes of rash behaviour. This holistic tactic underscores the need for behavioural reform rather than mere retribution. In schools, innovative methods are gaining ground. For example, rowdy students in UP schools are assigned such tasks as organising books or assisting peers. Meanwhile, creative punishments like rewriting lessons or engaging in debates channel energy constructively and emphasise growth over reprimand.
Discipline should not be about just imposing consequences but also guiding young minds toward self-awareness and societal contribution. Restorative justice, community service and counselling are replacing outdated corporal punishment, which often leaves emotional scars. Nevertheless, these reforms require collective commitment. Policymakers must institutionalise such practices, educators must adopt empathetic approaches and parents must support these efforts. Experts from NIMHANS (National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences) have stressed the importance of balancing love and limits at home to complement school-based initiatives.
Constructive discipline reflects the society’s recognition that youth’s missteps often stem from immaturity, not malice. By transforming mistakes into learning experiences, we not only shape better individuals but also foster a more compassionate community. It’s time to make responsibility the cornerstone of discipline, steering youth away from chaos and towards civic-mindedness. 
 What is the tone of the passage?
cpomains33.explanation:
C. (Correct): The passage presents facts and examples about disciplinary changes in India in a neutral and explanatory manner. It focuses on innovative approaches and policies, making the tone clearly informative. 
 A. (Incorrect): Although the passage discusses flaws in traditional disciplinary methods, it does not focus on criticizing them. Instead, it highlights solutions and reforms, which is not the focus of a critical tone. 
 B. (Incorrect): While the passage acknowledges progress and positive changes, it is primarily factual rather than emotional or hopeful. Optimism is a secondary element, not the main tone. 
 D. (Incorrect): There is no element of mockery, irony, or sarcasm in the passage. It maintains a serious and professional tone throughout.
